title.zh: 卷三百六十三 列傳第一百二十二 李光 許翰 許景衡 張愨 張所 陳禾 蔣猷
title.en: Volume 363 Biographies 122: Li Guang, Xu Han, Xu Jingheng, Zhang Que, Zhang Suo, Chen He, Jiang You
title.raw: 卷三百六十三 列傳第一百二十二 李光 許翰 許景衡 張愨 張所 陳禾 蔣猷 Volume 363 Biographies 122: Li Guang, Xu Han, Xu Jingheng, Zhang Que, Zhang Suo, Chen He, Jiang You

sentences.zh: 李光 許翰 許景衡 張愨 張所 陳禾 蔣猷

translations.literal: Li Guang, Xu Han, Xu Jingheng, Zhang Que, Zhang Suo, Chen He, Jiang You
translations.idiomatic: Li Guang, Xu Han, Xu Jingheng, Zhang Que, Zhang Suo, Chen He, and Jiang You

sentences.zh: 李光，字泰發，越州上虞人。

translations.literal: Li Guang, style name Taifa, was a man of Shangyu in Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guang, styled Taifa, was a native of Shangyu in Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 童稚不戲弄。

translations.literal: In childhood he did not play and frolic.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he shunned horseplay and frivolity.

sentences.zh: 父高稱曰：「吾兒雲間鶴，其興吾門乎！」

translations.literal: His father Gao said: "My son is a crane amid the clouds—will he not bring renown to our house!"
translations.idiomatic: His father Gao exclaimed, "My boy is a crane soaring above the clouds—surely he will bring glory to our clan!"

sentences.zh: 親喪，哀毀如成人，有致賻者，悉辭之。

translations.literal: When a parent died, his mourning and grief were like an adult's; those who offered funeral gifts he entirely declined.
translations.idiomatic: After a parent's death he mourned with the grief of a grown man and turned away every condolence gift offered him.

sentences.zh: 及葬，禮皆中節。

translations.literal: At the burial, every rite was properly measured.
translations.idiomatic: At the funeral every observance was conducted with exact propriety.

sentences.zh: 服除，遊太 學，登崇甯五年進士第。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he studied at the Imperial Academy and passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Chongning.
translations.idiomatic: Once his mourning was over, he entered the Imperial Academy and took the jinshi degree in the fifth year of the Chongning reign.

sentences.zh: 調開化令，有政聲，召赴都堂審察，時宰不悅，處以監當，改秩，知平江府常熟縣。

translations.literal: He was assigned as magistrate of Kaihua; his governance won praise, and he was summoned for review at the Court Bureau, but the chief ministers were displeased and placed him on supervisory duty with a rank change, as prefectural administrator of Changshu County in Pingjiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as magistrate of Kaihua, he earned a reputation for good government and was called to the Court Bureau for review; the chief ministers took offense, assigned him supervisory duty with a change of rank, and made him administrator of Changshu County in Pingjiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 朱勔父沖倚勢暴橫，光械治其家僮。

translations.literal: Zhu Mian's father Chong relied on his son's power and acted violently; Guang had his household servants shackled and tried.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mian's father Chong bullied others by leaning on his son's influence; Guang had Chong's household servants arrested and put in the stocks for trial.

sentences.zh: 沖怒，風部使者移 令吳江，光不為屈。

translations.literal: Chong was furious and had the ministry envoy transfer him as magistrate of Wujiang, but Guang would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Chong flew into a rage and had a ministry envoy hint that Guang should be transferred to Wujiang as magistrate, but Guang refused to bend.

sentences.zh: 改京東西學事司管勾文字。

translations.literal: He was changed to clerk for documents in the Directorate of Education for the Eastern and Western Capitals.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as a document clerk in the Eastern and Western Capitals Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 劉安世居南京，光以師禮見之。

translations.literal: Liu Anshi lived in Nanjing; Guang visited him with the courtesy due a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Anshi was living in Nanjing, Guang called on him with the deference owed a master.

sentences.zh: 安世告以所聞于溫公者曰：「學當自無妄中入。」

translations.literal: Anshi told him what he had heard from Master Wen, saying: "Learning should begin by entering through non-deception."
translations.idiomatic: Anshi passed on what he had learned from Master Wen (Sima Guang): "True learning must begin from the gate of sincerity—without self-deception."

sentences.zh: 光欣然領會。

translations.literal: Guang gladly received the teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Guang accepted the lesson with evident delight.

sentences.zh: 除太常博士，遷司封。

translations.literal: He was appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and transferred to the Bureau of Seals.
translations.idiomatic: He was made an Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and then moved to the Bureau of Seals.

sentences.zh: 首論士大夫諛佞成風，至妄引荀卿「有聽 從，無諫諍」之說，以杜塞言路；

translations.literal: He first argued that flattery and sycophancy had become the custom among scholar-officials, to the point of rashly citing Xunzi's saying "there is listening and following, but no remonstrance," in order to block the path of speech;
translations.idiomatic: In his first memorial he denounced the way scholar-officials had made flattery the norm, even twisting Xunzi's line that rulers "listen and obey but never hear remonstrance" into an excuse to shut down frank counsel;

sentences.zh: 又言怨嗟之氣，結為妖沴。

translations.literal: He also said that the air of resentment and lament had coalesced into uncanny calamities.
translations.idiomatic: He added that popular resentment had condensed into strange omens and disasters.

sentences.zh: 王黼惡之，令部注桂州陽朔縣。

translations.literal: Wang Fu hated this and had the ministry register him for Yangshuo County in Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu took offense and had the ministry assign him to Yangshuo County in Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 安世聞光以論事貶，貽書偉之。

translations.literal: When Anshi heard that Guang had been demoted for his memorials, he sent a letter praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Guang had been banished for speaking out, Anshi wrote to commend his courage.

sentences.zh: 李綱亦以論水災去國，居義興，伺光于 水驛，自出呼曰：「非越州李司封船乎？」

translations.literal: Li Gang had also left the capital after memorializing on the flood disaster and was living in Yixing; he waited for Guang at a river post, came out himself, and called: "Is this not the boat of Li of the Bureau of Seals from Yue Prefecture?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang, too, had been driven from court after memorializing about the floods and was staying in Yixing; he watched for Guang at a river station, stepped out, and hailed him: "Surely that is Vice Director Li from Yue Prefecture aboard?"

sentences.zh: 留數日，定交而別。

translations.literal: They stayed several days, formed a bond of friendship, and parted.
translations.idiomatic: They spent several days together, sealed their friendship, and went their separate ways.

sentences.zh: 除司勳員外郎，遷符寶郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director in the Bureau of Honors and transferred to Registrar of Tallies and Seals.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director in the Bureau of Honors and then Registrar of Tallies and Seals.

sentences.zh: 郭藥師叛，光知徽宗有內禪意，因納符，謂知樞密院蔡攸曰：「公家所為，皆咈眾心。

translations.literal: When Guo Yaoshi rebelled, Guang knew that Huizong intended to abdicate in favor of another; he therefore surrendered his tally and said to Cai You, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs: "What your family has done has all gone against the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Yaoshi turned traitor, Guang sensed that Huizong meant to abdicate; he handed in his seal of office and told Military Affairs Commissioner Cai You, "Everything your clan has done has defied the will of the people.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，非皇太子則國家俱危。」

translations.literal: In today's affair, if it is not the Crown Prince, then the state and the ruler will both be in peril."
translations.idiomatic: In the crisis we face today, unless the Crown Prince takes the throne, both sovereign and realm will be lost."

sentences.zh: 攸矍然，不敢為異。

translations.literal: You was startled and did not dare dissent.
translations.idiomatic: You blanched and dared raise no objection.

sentences.zh: 欽宗受禪，擢右 司諫。

translations.literal: When Qinzong received the abdication, Guang was promoted to Remonstrator of the Right Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After Qinzong accepted the throne, Guang was elevated to Remonstrator of the Right Bureau.

sentences.zh: 上皇東幸，憸人間兩宮，光請集議奉迎典禮。

translations.literal: When the Retired Emperor traveled east, crafty men sowed discord between the two palaces; Guang requested a joint deliberation on the rites for welcoming him back.
translations.idiomatic: When the Retired Emperor went east on his tour, schemers drove a wedge between the two courts; Guang asked that officials assemble to settle the protocol for receiving him back.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「東南財用，盡于朱勔，西北財用，困于李彥，天下根本之財，竭于蔡京、王黼。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Southeastern revenues have been exhausted by Zhu Mian; northwestern revenues have been strained by Li Yan; the fundamental wealth of the realm has been drained by Cai Jing and Wang Fu.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted: "The southeast's revenues have been swallowed by Zhu Mian; the northwest's coffers have been squeezed dry by Li Yan; and the empire's core finances have been bled white by Cai Jing and Wang Fu.

sentences.zh: 名為應奉，實入私室， 公家無半歲之儲，百姓無旬日之積。

translations.literal: Called tribute for the throne, it in fact entered private chambers; the public treasury has not half a year's stores, and the people have not ten days' savings.
translations.idiomatic: What was labeled imperial tribute in truth filled private vaults; the state lacks six months' reserves, and common households cannot scrape together ten days' provisions.

sentences.zh: 乞依舊制，三省、樞密院通知兵民財計，與戶部量一歲之出入，以制國用，選吏考核，使利源歸一。」

translations.literal: I beg that the old system be followed: let the Three Departments and the Bureau of Military Affairs jointly oversee military, civil, and fiscal affairs, reckon with the Ministry of Revenue the year's income and outgo to regulate state expenditure, select officials for inspection, and make revenue sources unified."
translations.idiomatic: I urge a return to precedent: let the Three Departments and the Bureau of Military Affairs coordinate military, civil, and fiscal planning; have the Ministry of Revenue tally annual receipts and disbursements to set national spending; appoint auditors to review accounts; and reunite every stream of revenue under one authority."

sentences.zh: 金人圍太原，援兵無功。

translations.literal: The Jurchens besieged Taiyuan and the relief armies achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Jurchen forces had Taiyuan under siege, and every relief column failed.

sentences.zh: 光言：「三鎮之地，祖宗百戰得之，一旦舉以與敵，何以為國？

translations.literal: Guang said: "The territory of the Three Prefectures was won by our forebears through a hundred battles; to hand it all at once to the enemy—how can we still call this a state?
translations.idiomatic: Guang argued: "Our ancestors won the Three Prefectures only after generations of bloodshed; if we surrender them wholesale to the enemy, what nation will be left for us to govern?

sentences.zh: 望詔大臣別議攻守之策，仍間道遣使檄河東、北兩路，盡起強壯策應，首尾掩擊。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will order the great ministers to deliberate separately on strategies of attack and defense, and also send envoys by secret routes with proclamations to the Eastern and Northern circuits of Hedong, raising all able-bodied men to coordinate relief and strike the enemy front and rear."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the throne command senior ministers to debate fresh plans for offense and defense, and that couriers be sent by hidden routes to rouse every able man in the Hedong eastern and northern circuits so they can strike the invaders from both ends."

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 時言者猶主王安石之學，詔榜廟堂。

translations.literal: At the time memorialists still upheld Wang Anshi's learning, and an edict was posted in the ancestral temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists were still championing Wang Anshi's doctrines, and an edict to that effect was posted in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 光又言：「祖宗規摹宏遠，安石欲盡廢法度，則謂人主制法而不當制於法；

translations.literal: Guang again said: "The founding design of our ancestors was vast and far-reaching; Anshi wished to abolish the laws entirely, and therefore said the ruler makes law and must not be constrained by law;
translations.idiomatic: Guang protested again: "Our founders laid plans on a grand scale; Anshi sought to sweep away every statute and argued that a sovereign makes law and must never be bound by it;

sentences.zh: 欲盡逐元老，則謂人主當化俗而不當化於俗。

translations.literal: wishing to drive out all the senior elders, he said the ruler should transform custom and must not be transformed by custom.
translations.idiomatic: and when he meant to purge every senior statesman, he insisted that the throne must reshape society rather than let society reshape the throne.

sentences.zh: 蔡京兄弟祖述其說，五十年間，毒流四海。

translations.literal: The Cai brothers followed and elaborated his doctrine; for fifty years its poison spread through the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: The Cai brothers took up and spread his teachings, and for fifty years their poison seeped into every corner of the realm.

sentences.zh: 今又風示中外，鼓惑民聽，豈朝廷之福？」

translations.literal: Now again you signal inside and outside the court, stirring and misleading the people's ears—can this be a blessing to the dynasty?"
translations.idiomatic: Now the court once more broadcasts this message at home and abroad, inflaming public opinion—how can that serve the dynasty's good?"

sentences.zh: 蔡攸欲以扈衛上皇行宮因緣入都，光奏：「攸若果入，則百姓必致生變，萬一驚犯屬車之塵，臣坐不預言之罪。

translations.literal: Cai You wished to use escorting the Retired Emperor's traveling palace as a pretext to enter the capital; Guang memorialized: "If You truly enters, the common people will surely stir up trouble; if by any chance the imperial carriage is startled, I shall bear the crime of not having forewarned it.
translations.idiomatic: Cai You planned to escort the Retired Emperor's mobile palace into the capital as a way to regain power; Guang wrote: "If You is allowed into the city, the populace will erupt; should the imperial procession be disturbed, I alone will bear blame for failing to warn of it.

sentences.zh: 望早黜責。」

translations.literal: I hope he will be dismissed and punished early."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that he be removed and punished without delay."

sentences.zh: 時已葺擷景園為甯德宮，而太上皇 後乃欲入居禁中。

translations.literal: By then Jiejing Garden had been repaired as Ningde Palace, yet the Retired Empress wished to move into the Forbidden City.
translations.idiomatic: Jiejing Garden had already been refurbished as Ningde Palace, yet the Retired Empress now wanted to take up residence inside the Forbidden City.

sentences.zh: 光奏：「禁中者，天子之宮。

translations.literal: Guang memorialized: "The Forbidden City is the Son of Heaven's dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Guang submitted: "The Forbidden City belongs to the reigning sovereign alone.

sentences.zh: 正使陛下欲便溫凊，奉迎入內，亦當躬稟上皇，下有司討論典禮。」

translations.literal: Even if Your Majesty wishes to attend to warmth and coolness in person and welcome her within, you should still report in person to the Retired Emperor and have the relevant offices deliberate the proper rites."
translations.idiomatic: Even if Your Majesty wishes to care for her comfort in person and bring her inside, you ought first to inform the Retired Emperor yourself and charge the proper offices with settling the ceremonial details."

sentences.zh: 乃下光章，使兩宮臣奏知，於是太上皇后居甯德 宮。

translations.literal: The emperor then issued Guang's memorial for the ministers of both palaces to report upward, and thereafter the Retired Empress dwelt in Ningde Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The throne circulated Guang's memorial for officials of both courts to relay upward, and the Retired Empress thereafter resided in Ningde Palace.

sentences.zh: 金人逼京城，士大夫委職而去者五十二人，罪同罰異，士論紛然，光請付理寺公行之。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens pressed the capital, fifty-two scholar-officials who abandoned their posts were punished differently for the same offense; opinion among the gentry was in uproar, and Guang asked that the case be handed to the Court of Judicial Review for uniform handling.
translations.idiomatic: As Jurchen armies closed on the capital, fifty-two officials who deserted their posts were punished unevenly for the same crime; public opinion seethed, and Guang urged that the Court of Judicial Review apply one standard to all.

sentences.zh: 太原圍急，奏：「乞就委折彥質盡起晉、絳、慈、隰、澤、潞、威勝、汾 八州民兵及本路諸縣弓手，俾守令各自部轄。

translations.literal: As the siege of Taiyuan grew urgent, he memorialized: "I beg that Zhe Yanzhi be entrusted at once to raise fully the militia of the eight prefectures Jin, Jiang, Ci, Xi, Ze, Lu, Weisheng, and Fen, together with the archer levies of every county on this circuit, and let the prefects and magistrates each command their own districts.
translations.idiomatic: With Taiyuan's plight worsening, he wrote: "Authorize Zhe Yanzhi immediately to mobilize every militiaman in Jin, Jiang, Ci, Xi, Ze, Lu, Weisheng, and Fen, along with county archer levies throughout the circuit, each district commander to lead his own men.

sentences.zh: 其土豪、士人願為首領者，假以初官、應副器甲，協力赴援。

translations.literal: For local strongmen and scholars willing to serve as leaders, grant them entry-level offices and supply armor and weapons, and let them join forces to march to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: Local magnates and gentry willing to lead should receive provisional rank, be furnished arms and armor, and march together to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 女真劫質親王，以三鎮為辭，勢必深入，請大修京城守禦 之備，以伐敵人之謀。」

translations.literal: The Jurchens have seized the imperial prince as hostage and demand the Three Prefectures as their price; they are sure to press deeper—please greatly strengthen the capital's defenses to thwart the enemy's designs."
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens hold an imperial prince hostage and demand the Three Prefectures; they will surely drive deeper inland. I urge a major overhaul of the capital's defenses to break their strategy."

sentences.zh: 又言：「朱勔托應奉脅制州縣，田園第宅，富擬王室。

translations.literal: He also said: "Zhu Mian, under the cover of imperial tribute offices, coerces prefectures and counties; his fields, gardens, mansions, and houses rival the wealth of the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Zhu Mian has used the tribute bureaucracy to bully prefectures and counties; his estates and mansions rival a prince's fortune.

sentences.zh: 乞擇清強官置司，追攝勔父子及奉承監司、守令，如胡直孺、盧宗原、陸寘、王促閔、趙霖、宋晦等，根勘驅磨，計資沒入，其強奪編戶產業者還之。」

translations.literal: I beg that upright, capable officials be chosen to establish an office, pursue and seize Mian and his father and the supervising commissioners and prefectural administrators who flattered them, such as Hu Zhiru, Lu Zongyuan, Lu Zhi, Wang Cumin, Zhao Lin, Song Hui, and others, investigate to the root and press for repayment, calculate assets for confiscation, and return what was forcibly seized from registered households."
translations.idiomatic: Appoint a bureau of upright, forceful officials to arrest Zhu Mian, his father, and the tribute commissioners and local magistrates who abetted them—men such as Hu Zhiru, Lu Zongyuan, Lu Zhi, Wang Cumin, Zhao Lin, and Song Hui—investigate every claim to the bottom, confiscate their wealth, and restore property wrested from registered households."

sentences.zh: 李會、李擢復以諫官召。

translations.literal: Li Hui and Li Zhuo were again summoned as remonstrating officials.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui and Li Zhuo were once more recalled to serve as remonstrators.

sentences.zh: 光奏：「蔡京復用，時會、擢迭為台官，禁不發一語；

translations.literal: Guang memorialized: "When Cai Jing was restored to power, Hui and Zhuo in turn served as censorial officials and were forbidden to utter a single word;
translations.idiomatic: Guang protested: "When Cai Jing returned to power, Hui and Zhuo took turns as censorial officers yet were barred from speaking a word of truth;

sentences.zh: 金人圍城，與白時中、李邦彥專主避敵割地之謀。

translations.literal: when the Jurchens besieged the city, they joined Bai Shizhong and Li Bangyan in exclusively advocating avoiding the enemy and ceding territory.
translations.idiomatic: when the Jurchens encircled the capital they sided with Bai Shizhong and Li Bangyan in pushing only to flee the foe and surrender land.

sentences.zh: 時中、邦彥坐是落職，而會、擢反被召用，復預諫諍之列。

translations.literal: Shizhong and Bangyan lost their posts on this account, yet Hui and Zhuo were instead recalled and again entered the ranks of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong and Bangyan lost office for that very policy, yet Hui and Zhuo are rewarded with recall and seats among the remonstrators again.

sentences.zh: 乞寢成命。」

translations.literal: I beg that the completed appointment be suspended."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that these appointments be revoked."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 光丐外，亦不報。

translations.literal: Guang begged for an outside post; again there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Guang asked to be sent out of the capital; again he received no reply.

sentences.zh: 彗出寅、艮間，耿南仲輩皆謂應在外夷，不足憂。

translations.literal: A comet appeared between the constellations Yin and Gen; Geng Nanzhong and his party all said it portended foreign barbarians and was not worth worry.
translations.idiomatic: A comet rose between the Yin and Gen asterisms; Geng Nanzhong and his allies insisted it foretold trouble among foreign tribes and was no cause for alarm.

sentences.zh: 光奏：「孔子作《春秋》，不書祥瑞者，蓋欲使人君恐懼修省，未聞以災異歸之外夷也。」

translations.literal: Guang memorialized: "When Confucius compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals, he did not record auspicious omens because he wished to make rulers fearful and self-correcting; one has never heard of attributing calamities and anomalies to foreign barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: Guang wrote: "Confucius left auspicious signs out of the Spring and Autumn Annals so that rulers would tremble and reform themselves; I have never heard of blaming heaven's warnings on barbarians beyond the frontier."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，監汀州酒稅。

translations.literal: After the memorial was submitted, he was made supervisor of the wine tax at Ting Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When his memorial went in, he was demoted to supervisor of the wine tax at Ting Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，擢秘書少監，除知江州；

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, Guang was promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Library and appointed prefect of Jiang Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong ascended the throne, Guang was made Vice Director of the Palace Library and appointed prefect of Jiang Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢侍御史，皆以道梗不赴。

translations.literal: before long he was promoted to Attending Censor, but in both cases the roads were blocked and he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: soon afterward he was named Attending Censor, yet in each case war-blocked roads kept him from taking up the post.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，車駕自臨安移蹕建康，除知宣州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan the imperial carriage moved its encampment from Lin'an to Jiankang, and he was appointed prefect of Xuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyan, as the court shifted from Lin'an to Jiankang, he was made prefect of Xuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時範瓊將過軍，光先入視事，瓊至則開門延 勞，留三日而去，無敢嘩者。

translations.literal: At the time Fan Qiong was about to pass through with his army; Guang entered first to take up office, and when Qiong arrived he opened the gates to welcome and refresh the troops; they stayed three days and departed, and none dared make an uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Qiong's army was due to march through; Guang took office ahead of them, and when Qiong arrived Guang opened the gates to welcome and provision his men. They stayed three days and moved on without a single riot.

sentences.zh: 光以宣密邇行都，乃繕城池，聚兵糧，籍六邑之民，保伍相比，謂之義社。

translations.literal: Guang considered that Xuan lay close to the traveling capital and therefore repaired the walls, gathered arms and grain, registered the people of the six districts, linked them in mutual-security groups of five households, and called this the Righteous Societies.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xuan lay near the mobile court, Guang repaired the walls, stockpiled arms and grain, enrolled the people of six counties in linked mutual-security groups he called Righteous Societies.

sentences.zh: 擇其健武者，統以土豪，得保甲萬餘，號「精揀軍」。

translations.literal: He chose the sturdy and martial among them, placed local strongmen in command, and mustered more than ten thousand militia, which he titled the "Elite Picked Army."
translations.idiomatic: From their ranks he picked the sturdiest fighters, placed local leaders in command, and raised more than ten thousand militiamen under the name Elite Picked Army.

sentences.zh: 又柵 險要二十三所謹戍之，厘城止為十地分，分巡內外，晝則自便，夜則守城，有警則戰。

translations.literal: He also palisaded twenty-three strategic points and garrisoned them carefully, divided the city proper into ten sectors, patrolled inside and outside separately, allowed free movement by day, guarded the walls by night, and fought when there was alarm.
translations.idiomatic: He fortified twenty-three choke points, divided the city into ten wards with separate patrols inside and out, let residents move freely by day, manned the walls at night, and sent fighters out at the first alarm.

sentences.zh: 苗租歲輸邑者，悉命輸郡。

translations.literal: The seedling tax yearly delivered to the districts he ordered all sent to the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: He redirected every district's annual seedling-tax payment to the prefectural treasury.

sentences.zh: 初歡言不便，及守城之日，贍軍養民，迄賴以濟。

translations.literal: At first Huan said it was inconvenient, but when the day came to defend the city, provisioning the army and sustaining the people all depended on this measure to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Huan had first complained that the policy was impractical, yet when siege came it was what kept the army fed and the people alive.

sentences.zh: 事聞，授管內安撫，許便宜從事，進直龍圖閣。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was made Pacification Commissioner within the circuit, permitted to act as circumstances required, and advanced to the Dragon Diagram Hall as a direct appointee.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was named Pacification Commissioner for the circuit with discretionary authority and promoted to direct appointee of the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 杜充以建康降，金人奪馬家渡。

translations.literal: Du Chong surrendered Jiankang to the Jurchens, and the Jurchens seized Majia Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chong handed Jiankang over to the Jurchens, who then took Majia Ford.

sentences.zh: 御營統制王曁燮、王曁民素不相能，至是，擁潰兵砦城外索鬥。

translations.literal: Imperial Camp controllers Wang Siye and Wang Simin had never been on good terms; at this time they gathered routed troops and encamped outside the city demanding a fight.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Camp commanders Wang Siye and Wang Simin had long been at odds; now they massed routed soldiers outside the walls and challenged each other to battle.

sentences.zh: 光親至營，諭以先國家後私讎之義，皆感悟解去。

translations.literal: Guang went in person to the camps and admonished them with the principle of putting the state before private enmity; all were moved to understanding and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Guang went to both camps in person and urged them to place the realm before private vendetta; moved, they broke camp and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時奔將、散卒 至者，光悉厚貲給遺。

translations.literal: At the time fleeing generals and scattered soldiers who arrived were all given generous gifts and sent on their way.
translations.idiomatic: Every routed officer or stray soldier who reached Xuan received a generous stipend and was sent on his way.

sentences.zh: 有水軍叛於繁昌，逼宣境，即遣兵援擊，出賊不意，遂宵遁。

translations.literal: When naval forces rebelled at Fanchang and pressed the border of Xuan, he immediately sent troops to strike in support, catching the bandits unawares so that they fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel sailors at Fanchang threatened Xuan's border, he sent troops at once, took them by surprise, and drove them to flee under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 進右文殿修撰。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Compiler of the Hall of Literary Glory on the Right.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Compiler of the Right Hall of Literary Glory.

sentences.zh: 光奏：「金人雖深入江、浙，然違天時地利，臣已移文劉光世領 大兵赴州，並力攻討。

translations.literal: Guang memorialized: "Although the Jurchens have penetrated deeply into Jiang and Zhe, they violate the season and terrain; I have already sent a dispatch to Liu Guangshi to lead a great army to this prefecture and join forces in attack.
translations.idiomatic: Guang wrote: "The Jurchens may have plunged deep into Jiangsu and Zhejiang, but they fight against season and terrain; I have already ordered Liu Guangshi to march a main force here for a joint offensive.

sentences.zh: 乞速委宣撫使周望，約日水陸並進。」

translations.literal: I beg that Pacification Commissioner Zhou Wang be quickly entrusted and a day fixed for simultaneous advance by land and water."
translations.idiomatic: I urge that Pacification Commissioner Zhou Wang be empowered at once and a date set for a coordinated land-and-water advance."

sentences.zh: 潰將邵青自真州擁舟數百艘，剽當塗、蕪湖兩邑間，光招諭之，遺米二千斛。

translations.literal: The routed general Shao Qing from Zhen Prefecture led several hundred boats and plundered between the two districts of Dangtu and Wuhu; Guang summoned and instructed him and sent two thousand bushels of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Routed general Shao Qing sailed from Zhen Prefecture with hundreds of boats and raided between Dangtu and Wuhu; Guang won him over with persuasion and sent two thousand bushels of rice.

sentences.zh: 青喜，謂使者曰：「我官軍也，所過皆以盜賊見遇，獨李公不疑我。」

translations.literal: Qing was pleased and said to the envoy: "I am imperial troops; everywhere I pass I am treated as bandits, yet Lord Li alone does not doubt me."
translations.idiomatic: Qing was delighted and told the envoy, "We are imperial soldiers, yet everywhere we go people treat us as bandits—only Lord Li trusts us."

sentences.zh: 於是秋毫無犯。

translations.literal: Thereafter not even an autumn hair was harmed.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his men did not take so much as a blade of grain.

sentences.zh: 他日，舟過繁昌，或紿之曰：「宣境也。」

translations.literal: Another day, when his boats passed Fanchang, someone deceived him, saying: "This is Xuan territory."
translations.idiomatic: Later, as his fleet passed Fanchang, someone tricked him into thinking he had entered Xuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乃掠北岸而去。

translations.literal: He then plundered the north bank and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He raided the north bank instead and sailed away.

sentences.zh: 劇盜戚方破甯國縣，抵城下，分兵四擊。

translations.literal: The fierce bandit Qi Fang broke Ningguo County, reached below the city walls, and divided his troops to attack from four sides.
translations.idiomatic: The notorious bandit Qi Fang overran Ningguo County, advanced to the walls of Xuan, and assaulted from four directions at once.

sentences.zh: 光募勇敢劫之，賊驚擾，自相屠蹂。

translations.literal: Guang recruited the brave to raid them; the bandits were startled and thrown into confusion and slaughtered one another.
translations.idiomatic: Guang sent bold raiders against them; the rebels panicked and turned on one another in the dark.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣統制官巨師古、劉晏兼程來援。

translations.literal: The court dispatched control officers Ju Shigu and Liu Yan to hurry to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent control officers Ju Shigu and Liu Yan to race to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 賊急攻朝京門，纜竹木為浮梁以濟。

translations.literal: The bandits pressed the attack on Chaojing Gate, lashed bamboo and timber into a floating bridge to cross.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels stormed Chaojing Gate and lashed together a pontoon bridge of bamboo and timber to cross the moat.

sentences.zh: 須臾， 軍傅城，列炮具，立石對樓。

translations.literal: In a moment the army reached the wall, arrayed catapults, and erected stone counter-towers.
translations.idiomatic: Within moments their forces pressed the wall, set up stone-throwers, and raised siege towers opposite the battlements.

sentences.zh: 光命編竹若簾揭之，炮至即反墜，不能傷。

translations.literal: Guang ordered bamboo woven like curtains hung up; when stones arrived they rebounded and fell back, and could not harm.
translations.idiomatic: Guang had bamboo matting hung like curtains so that when boulders struck they bounced back and inflicted no damage.

sentences.zh: 取桱木為撞竿，倚女牆以禦對樓，賊引卻。

translations.literal: He took banyan wood for battering poles, leaned them on the parapet to counter the enemy towers, and the bandits drew back.
translations.idiomatic: He fashioned battering beams from banyan trunks, braced them on the parapet to smash the enemy towers, and the rebels pulled back.

sentences.zh: 劉晏率赤心隊直搗其砦，賊陽退，晏追之，伏發 遇害。

translations.literal: Liu Yan led the Red-Heart Company straight against their camp; the bandits feigned retreat, Yan pursued, an ambush sprang up, and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan led the Red-Heart Company in a direct assault on their camp; the rebels feigned retreat, then sprang an ambush and killed him as he pursued.

sentences.zh: 師古以中軍大破賊，賊遁去。

translations.literal: Shigu with the central army greatly defeated the bandits, and the bandits fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu's main force routed the rebels, who fled the field.

sentences.zh: 初，戚方圍宣，與其副並馬巡城，指畫攻具。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qi Fang besieged Xuan, he and his lieutenant rode side by side around the wall, pointing out siege engines.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier in the siege Qi Fang and his lieutenant had ridden abreast around the walls, directing the placement of siege engines.

sentences.zh: 光以書傅矢射其副馬前，言：「戚方窮寇，天誅必加，汝為將家子，何至附賊。」

translations.literal: Guang attached a letter to an arrow and shot it before the lieutenant's horse, saying: "Qi Fang is a cornered bandit; heaven's punishment is sure to fall—you are the son of a general's house, how can you attach yourself to bandits?"
translations.idiomatic: Guang tied a letter to an arrow and shot it to the lieutenant's feet: "Qi Fang is a doomed outlaw whom heaven will surely destroy—you are born to a general's line; why side with rebels?"

sentences.zh: 二人相疑，攻稍緩，始得為備，而援師至矣。

translations.literal: The two men grew suspicious of each other, the attack slackened somewhat, and only then could preparations be made, while relief troops arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The two men began to mistrust each other, the assault slowed, Guang finally had time to prepare his defenses, and relief troops arrived.

sentences.zh: 嘗置匕首枕匣中，與家人約曰：「城不可必保，若使人取匕首，我必死。

translations.literal: He once placed a dagger in the pillow box and made an agreement with his family, saying: "The city cannot be surely preserved; if someone is sent to fetch the dagger, I shall certainly die.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a dagger in his pillow case and told his household: "The city may fall; if anyone is sent for that dagger, know that I mean to die.

sentences.zh: 汝輩宜自殺，無落賊手。」

translations.literal: You should kill yourselves and not fall into the bandits' hands."
translations.idiomatic: You must take your own lives rather than fall into the rebels' hands."

sentences.zh: 除徽猷閣待制、知 臨安府。

translations.literal: He was appointed Awaiting Draftsman of the Hall of Literary Eminence and prefect of Lin'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Awaiting Draftsman of the Hall of Literary Eminence and prefect of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年正月，除知洪州，固辭，提舉臨安府洞霄宮。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Shaoxing he was appointed prefect of Hong Prefecture; he firmly declined and was made intendant of the Dongxiao Palace in Lin'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Shaoxing 1 he was offered Hong Prefecture but firmly declined, accepting instead the sinecure of intendant of the Dongxiao Palace near Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 除知婺州，甫至郡，擢吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Wu Prefecture; as soon as he reached the commandery he was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Named prefect of Wu, he had barely arrived when he was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 光奏疏極論朋黨之害：「議論之臣，各懷顧避，莫肯以持危扶顛為己 任。

translations.literal: Guang memorialized at length on the harm of faction: "Memorializing officials each harbor concern for themselves and shrink back, none willing to take holding up a tottering state and righting a fallen order as their own duty.
translations.idiomatic: Guang submitted a long memorial on the evils of faction: "Censors and remonstrators look out for themselves and hold back, unwilling to shoulder the task of saving a dynasty on the brink.

sentences.zh: 駐蹕會稽，首尾三載。

translations.literal: The imperial encampment was at Kuaiji for three years from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: The court had been encamped at Kuaiji for three full years.

sentences.zh: 自去秋迄今，敵人無復南渡之意，淮甸咫尺，了不經營，長江千里，不為限制，惴惴焉日為乘桴浮海之計。

translations.literal: From last autumn until now the enemy has shown no further intent to cross south; the Huai region is within a stone's throw yet not managed at all; the Yangzi's thousand li are left unrestricted; trembling daily they make plans to take a raft and flee across the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Since last autumn the enemy has shown no sign of crossing south again, yet the Huai frontier lies at our doorstep and goes utterly neglected; the thousand-li Yangzi is undefended; and the court trembles daily over plans to take ship and flee overseas.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝區區草創，猶能立宗 社，修宮闕，保江、浙。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Jin, in his small beginnings, still could establish the ancestral altars, repair palaces and halls, and preserve Jiang and Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Jin began with a tiny foothold, yet still restored the altars of state, rebuilt palaces, and held Jiang and Zhe.

sentences.zh: 劉琨、祖逖與逆胡拒戰于並、冀、兗、豫、司、雍諸州，未嘗陷沒也。

translations.literal: Liu Kun and Zu Ti resisted the rebel barbarians in battle across the prefectures of Bing, Ji, Yan, Yu, Si, and Yong, and those regions were never wholly lost.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun and Zu Ti fought the northern invaders across Bing, Ji, Yan, Yu, Si, and Yong, and those heartland provinces were never entirely lost.

sentences.zh: 石季龍重兵已至曆陽，命王導都督中外諸軍以禦之，未聞專主避狄如 今日也。

translations.literal: When Shi Jilong's heavy forces had already reached Liyang, Wang Dao was ordered to command all armies inside and outside the court to resist them; one never heard of exclusively advocating avoiding the barbarians as today.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Hu's main army reached Liyang, the court ordered Wang Dao to command all forces against him—not to preach flight from the barbarians, as our ministers do today.

sentences.zh: 陛下駐蹕會稽，江、浙為根本之地，使進足以戰、退足以守者，莫如建康。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's encampment is at Kuaiji; Jiang and Zhe are the root lands; for a place where advance is sufficient to fight and retreat sufficient to defend, none is like Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is encamped at Kuaiji while Jiang and Zhe remain our foundation; for a capital where we can advance to fight and retreat to hold, nothing surpasses Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 建康至姑熟一百八十里，其隘可守者有六：曰江寧鎮，曰鹈岡砂夾，曰採石，曰 大信，其上則有蕪湖、繁昌，皆與淮南對境。

translations.literal: From Jiankang to Gushu is one hundred eighty li; the passes that can be defended are six: called Jiangning Post, Tigeang Shajia, Caishi, Daxin, and above these Wuhu and Fanchang, all facing Huainan across the border.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang lies one hundred eighty li from Gushu; six choke points can be held—Jiangning Post, Tigeang Shajia, Caishi, Daxin, and upstream Wuhu and Fanchang—all facing Huainan across the river.

sentences.zh: 其餘皆蘆簖之場，或鹈奇岸水勢湍悍，難施舟楫。

translations.literal: The rest are reed-fence shallows, or places where the current runs fierce along strange banks, difficult for boats and oars.
translations.idiomatic: Elsewhere lie reed marshes and stretches where the current runs too fierce for fleets to pass.

sentences.zh: 莫若預于諸隘屯兵積粟，命將士各管地分，調發旁近鄉兵，協力守 禦。

translations.literal: Better to station troops and store grain beforehand at every pass, order officers and soldiers each to administer a sector, mobilize nearby village militia, and join forces in defense.
translations.idiomatic: We should pre-position troops and grain at each pass, assign officers to sectors, mobilize local militia, and coordinate the defense.

sentences.zh: 乞明詔大臣，參酌施行。」

translations.literal: I beg that Your Majesty clearly command the great ministers to deliberate and carry this out."
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to order the senior ministers to study this plan and put it into effect."

sentences.zh: 時有詔，金人深入，諸郡守臣相度，或守或避，令得自便。

translations.literal: At the time there was an edict: as the Jurchens penetrated deeply, prefectural administrators were to assess whether to hold or flee and were permitted to choose as they saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then allowed every prefect to decide for himself whether to hold or flee as the Jurchens advanced.

sentences.zh: 光言：「守臣任人民、社稷之重，固當存亡以之。

translations.literal: Guang said: "Administrators bear the weight of the people and the altars of state; they should naturally live or die with them.
translations.idiomatic: Guang argued: "Local officials hold the lives of the people and the fate of the altars in their hands; they must stand or fall with their posts.

sentences.zh: 若預開遷避之門，是誘之遁也，願追寢前詔。」

translations.literal: If you open in advance a door to relocation and avoidance, you are enticing them to flee; I hope the previous edict will be urgently suspended."
translations.idiomatic: Opening an escape route in advance only invites flight; I beg that the earlier edict be withdrawn at once."

sentences.zh: 上 欲移蹕臨安，被旨節制臨安府見屯諸軍，兼戶部侍郎、督營繕事。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to move the encampment to Lin'an; Guang received orders to control all armies then stationed in Lin'an Prefecture, and concurrently served as Vice Minister of Revenue overseeing construction and repairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned to move the court to Lin'an, Guang was ordered to take command of all troops stationed there, while also serving as Vice Minister of Revenue in charge of construction.

sentences.zh: 光經營撙節，不擾而辦。

translations.literal: Guang managed affairs with thrift; without disturbing the people he completed everything.
translations.idiomatic: Guang ran the work frugally and finished every task without troubling the populace.

sentences.zh: 奏蠲減二浙積負及九邑科配，以示施德自近之意。

translations.literal: He memorialized to remit accumulated arrears in the two Zhe circuits and tax levies in nine districts, to show the intent of bestowing grace beginning close at hand.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to cancel accumulated tax debts in Zhejiang and levies in nine districts, showing that mercy should begin at home.

sentences.zh: 戚方以管軍屬節制，甚 懼，拜庭下。

translations.literal: Qi Fang, whose commanded troops now fell under Guang's control, was greatly afraid and prostrated himself in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Fang, now under Guang's command, was terrified and kowtowed in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 光握手起之，曰：「公昔為盜，某為守，分當相直；

translations.literal: Guang took his hand and raised him, saying: "You were once a bandit and I was the administrator; by our stations we were bound to oppose each other;
translations.idiomatic: Guang took his hand and lifted him up, saying, "Once you were a rebel and I was the prefect—we were fated to stand against each other;

sentences.zh: 今俱為臣子，當共勉力忠義，勿以前事為疑。」

translations.literal: now we are both subjects; we should together exert ourselves in loyalty and righteousness and not let past affairs breed suspicion."
translations.idiomatic: now we are both servants of the throne; let us devote ourselves to loyalty and leave the past behind."

sentences.zh: 方謝且泣。

translations.literal: Fang thanked him and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Fang thanked him through tears.

sentences.zh: 兼侍讀，因奏：「金人內寇，百姓失業 為盜賊，本非獲已，尚可誠感。

translations.literal: Concurrently serving as Lecturer-in-Waiting, he memorialized: "When the Jurchens invade within, the people lose their livelihoods and become bandits; they do not do so willingly, and can still be moved by sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: As Lecturer-in-Waiting he added: "Jurchen raids have driven the people to banditry against their will; many can still be won back by honest persuasion.

sentences.zh: 自李成北走，群盜離心，儻因斯時顯用一二酋豪，以風厲其黨，必更相效慕，以次就降。」

translations.literal: Since Li Cheng fled north, the bandit bands have lost heart; if at this moment one or two chieftains were openly employed to set an example for their factions, they would surely emulate one another in turn and submit in sequence."
translations.idiomatic: Since Li Cheng fled north the rebel bands have lost cohesion; if we now elevate a few chieftains as examples, the rest will follow and surrender one after another."

sentences.zh: 擢吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 大將韓世清本苗傅餘黨，久屯宣城，擅據倉庫，調發不行。

translations.literal: The great general Han Shiqing was originally a remnant of Miao Fu's faction; he had long been stationed at Xuancheng, seized the granaries on his own authority, and would not obey requisitions.
translations.idiomatic: General Han Shiqing, a holdover from Miao Fu's mutiny, had camped at Xuancheng for years, seized the granaries, and ignored every requisition.

sentences.zh: 光請先事除之，乃授光淮西招撫使。

translations.literal: Guang asked to remove him first; he was then appointed Pacification Commissioner of Huai West.
translations.idiomatic: Guang asked leave to deal with him first and was named Pacification Commissioner of Huai West.

sentences.zh: 光假道至郡，世清入謁，縛送闕下伏誅。

translations.literal: Guang took a detour to reach the commandery; Shiqing came to pay his respects and was bound and sent to the capital, where he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Guang traveled by a roundabout route to the prefecture; Shiqing came to pay his respects, was seized, sent to the capital, and executed.

sentences.zh: 初，光於上前面稟成 算，宰相以不預聞，怒之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Guang had reported his completed plan before the emperor's face; the chief minister, not having been informed beforehand, was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Guang had laid his plan before the emperor in person; the chief minister, not having been consulted, was furious.

sentences.zh: 未至，道除端明殿學士、江東安撫大使、知建康府、壽春滁濠廬和無為宣撫使。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, en route he was appointed Academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity, Grand Pacification Commissioner of Jiang East, prefect of Jiankang, and Pacification Commissioner of Shouchun, Chuzhou, Haozhou, Luzhou, Hezhou, and Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, he was named Academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity, Grand Pacification Commissioner of Jiang East, prefect of Jiankang, and Pacification Commissioner over Shouchun, Chuzhou, Haozhou, Luzhou, Hezhou, and Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 時太平州卒陸德囚守臣據城叛，光多設方略，盡擒其黨。

translations.literal: At the time the soldier Lu De of Taiping Prefecture imprisoned the administrator, seized the city, and rebelled; Guang devised many stratagems and captured all his followers.
translations.idiomatic: When a Taiping garrison soldier named Lu De imprisoned the prefect and seized the city, Guang devised several stratagems and captured the entire rebel band.

sentences.zh: 秦檜既罷，呂頤浩、朱勝非並相，光議論素與不合。

translations.literal: After Qin Hui was dismissed, Lü Yihao and Zhu Shengfei both became chief ministers; Guang's views had long been at odds with theirs.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin Hui fell, Lü Yihao and Zhu Shengfei shared power as chief ministers—men with whom Guang had long disagreed.

sentences.zh: 言者指光為檜黨，落職奉祠。

translations.literal: Memorialists pointed to Guang as a member of Hui's faction; he lost his post and was assigned to temple service.
translations.idiomatic: Critics denounced him as a Qin Hui partisan; he was demoted to a temple sinecure.

sentences.zh: 尋復寶文閣待制、知湖州，除顯謨閣直學士，移守平江，除禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was restored as Awaiting Draftsman of the Hall of Literary Treasures and prefect of Hu Prefecture, appointed Direct Academician of the Hall of Manifest Counsel, transferred to guard Pingjiang, and made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as Awaiting Draftsman of the Hall of Literary Treasures and prefect of Hu, made Direct Academician of the Hall of Manifest Counsel, transferred to Pingjiang, and appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 光言： 「自古創業中興，必有所因而起。

translations.literal: Guang said: "From antiquity, founding a state or restoring a dynasty has always depended on some foundation from which to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Guang observed: "Every dynasty founded or restored has risen from a secure base.

sentences.zh: 漢高因關中，光武因河內，駐蹕東南，兩浙非根本所因之地乎？

translations.literal: Gaozu of Han relied on Guanzhong, Guangwu of Han relied on Henei—Your Majesty's encampment is in the southeast; are not the two Zhe circuits the foundational ground on which to rely?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu drew strength from Guanzhong and Guangwu from Henei; with the court in the southeast, are not the two Zhe circuits our natural foundation?

sentences.zh: 自冬及春，雨雪不已，百姓失業，乞選台諫察實以聞。

translations.literal: From winter into spring rain and snow did not cease; the people lost their livelihoods; he begged that censors and remonstrators be chosen to investigate the facts and report.
translations.idiomatic: Rain and snow had fallen without pause from winter into spring, leaving the people destitute; he asked that censors be sent to verify conditions and report back.

sentences.zh: 兼比歲福 建、湖南盜作，範汝為、楊麼相挺而起，朝廷發大兵誅討，殺戮過當。

translations.literal: Moreover, in recent years bandits have risen in Fujian and Hunan; Fan Ruwei and Yang Yao have risen one after another; the court has sent great armies to suppress them, with killing beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile banditry had flared in Fujian and Hunan; Fan Ruwei and Yang Yao had risen in succession, and the court's punitive campaigns had slaughtered far too many.

sentences.zh: 今諸路旱荒，流丐滿路，盜賊出入。

translations.literal: Now every circuit suffers drought and famine; refugees begging fill the roads, and bandits come and go.
translations.idiomatic: Now drought and famine afflict every circuit; beggars choke the highways and bandits roam freely.

sentences.zh: 宜選良吏招懷撫納，責諸路監司按貪贓，恤流殍。」

translations.literal: Good officials should be chosen to win over, comfort, and accept them; circuit supervisors should be charged to investigate corruption and embezzlement and relieve the wandering dead."
translations.idiomatic: Send capable officials to win rebels back by kindness, order circuit supervisors to prosecute corruption, and relieve the starving refugees."

sentences.zh: 議臣欲推行四川交子法于江、浙，光言：「有錢則交子可行。

translations.literal: Deliberating officials wished to extend the Sichuan jiaozi system to Jiang and Zhe; Guang said: "If there is cash backing, jiaozi can work.
translations.idiomatic: Some ministers wanted to extend Sichuan's jiaozi paper money to Jiang and Zhe; Guang replied, "Jiaozi only works when it is fully backed by coin.

sentences.zh: 今已謂樁辦若干錢，行若干交子，此議者欲朝廷欺陛下，使陛下異時不免欺百姓也。

translations.literal: Now they say a certain sum of cash is to be set aside and a certain amount of jiaozi issued—those who advocate this wish the court to deceive Your Majesty, so that Your Majesty in time cannot avoid deceiving the common people.
translations.idiomatic: They claim a reserve will be set aside while issuing notes regardless—such men would have the court deceive Your Majesty now so that you must deceive the people later.

sentences.zh: 若已樁辦見 錢，則目今所行錢關子，已是通快，何至紛紛？

translations.literal: If ready cash has truly been set aside, then the cash notes now in circulation already circulate smoothly—why all this clamor?
translations.idiomatic: If coin reserves truly exist, the cash notes already in circulation work well enough—why stir up this controversy?

sentences.zh: 其工部鑄到交子務銅印，臣未敢給降。」

translations.literal: The copper seal cast by the Ministry of Works for the Jiaozi Office—I have not dared to issue it."
translations.idiomatic: As for the copper seal the Ministry of Works cast for the Jiaozi Office, I have refused to release it."

sentences.zh: 除端明殿學士，守台州，俄改溫州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity and ordered to guard Taizhou; soon he was changed to Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity and sent to guard Taizhou, then soon transferred to Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 劉光世、張俊連以捷聞。

translations.literal: Liu Guangshi and Zhang Jun reported victories in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangshi and Zhang Jun sent news of victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 光言：「觀金人佈置，必有主謀。

translations.literal: Guang said: "Judging from the Jurchens' disposition, there must be a master strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Guang warned: "From the Jurchens' deployments, someone is clearly directing them.

sentences.zh: 今已據東南形勢，敵人萬里遠來，利於速戰，宜戒諸將持重以老之。

translations.literal: They now hold the strategic terrain of the southeast; the enemy has come ten thousand li from afar and profits from swift battle—generals should be warned to act with weight and wear them down.
translations.idiomatic: They now hold the southeast's strategic ground; the enemy has marched ten thousand li and needs a quick fight—our generals must be warned to stand firm and wear them down.

sentences.zh: 不過數月，彼食盡，則勝算在我矣。」

translations.literal: In no more than a few months their provisions will be exhausted, and the odds of victory will be ours."
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months their supplies will run out, and victory will be ours."

sentences.zh: 除江西安撫、知洪州兼制置大使，擢吏部尚書，逾月，除參知政事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Jiang West, prefect of Hong Prefecture and concurrently Grand Commissioner for Military Affairs, promoted to Minister of Personnel, and after a month made Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Pacification Commissioner of Jiang West, prefect of Hong and Grand Commissioner for Military Affairs, promoted to Minister of Personnel, and a month later made Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 時秦檜初定和議，將揭榜，欲籍光名鎮壓。

translations.literal: At the time Qin Hui had just settled the peace agreement and was about to post the proclamation; he wished to borrow Guang's name to suppress dissent.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui had just finalized the peace treaty and planned to post the public notice; he wanted Guang's prestige to silence opposition.

sentences.zh: 上意不欲用光，檜言：「光有人望，若同押榜，浮議自息。」

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was not inclined to use Guang; Hui said: "Guang enjoys public esteem; if he countersigns the proclamation together, loose talk will quiet of itself."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was reluctant to use him, but Hui argued: "Guang commands public respect; if he countersigns the notice, idle criticism will die down."

sentences.zh: 遂用之。

translations.literal: He was therefore employed.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was brought in.

sentences.zh: 同郡楊煒上光書，責以附時相取尊官，墮黠虜 奸計，隳平時大節。

translations.literal: Yang Wei of the same commandery sent Guang a letter rebuking him for attaching himself to the chief minister to gain high office, falling into the crafty barbarians' treacherous scheme, and destroying his usual great integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wei, a fellow townsman, wrote to rebuke him for currying favor with the chief minister, falling into the Jurchens' trap, and betraying his lifelong integrity.

sentences.zh: 光本意謂但可因和而為自治之計。

translations.literal: Guang's original intent was that one could use the peace only as a basis for plans of self-strengthening governance.
translations.idiomatic: Guang had meant only to use the truce as breathing space to rebuild the state.

sentences.zh: 既而檜議徹淮南守備，奪諸將兵權，光極言戎狄狼子野心，和不可恃，備不可徹。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Hui proposed withdrawing Huainan defenses and stripping generals of military authority; Guang spoke urgently that the northern barbarians have the nature of wolf cubs and cannot be trusted, that peace cannot be relied on, and that defenses cannot be withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui then proposed stripping Huainan's garrisons and disarming the generals, Guang protested fiercely that the northern tribes are treacherous by nature, peace cannot be trusted, and defenses must not be dismantled.

sentences.zh: 檜惡之。

translations.literal: Hui hated him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Hui came to hate him.

sentences.zh: 檜以親黨鄭億年為 資政殿學士，光于榻前面折之，又與檜語難上前，因曰：「觀檜之意，是欲壅蔽陛下耳目，盜弄國權，懷奸誤國，不可不察。」

translations.literal: Hui made his kinsman Zheng Yinian an Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance; Guang rebuked this before the emperor's couch, and again disputed with Hui in the emperor's presence, saying: "Judging Hui's intent, he wishes to block up Your Majesty's ears and eyes, steal and manipulate state power, harbor treachery and harm the state—this cannot go unexamined."
translations.idiomatic: When Hui appointed his protégé Zheng Yinian to the Hall for Assisting Governance, Guang openly rebuked the move before the emperor and again confronted Hui in court: "Hui means to blind Your Majesty, seize state power, and ruin the country through treachery—you must see through him."

sentences.zh: 檜大怒，明日，光丐去。

translations.literal: Hui was greatly enraged; the next day Guang begged to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Hui flew into a rage; the next day Guang asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 高宗曰： 「卿昨面叱秦檜，舉措如古人。

translations.literal: Gaozong said: "Yesterday you rebuked Qin Hui to his face; your conduct was like the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong said, "Yesterday you scolded Qin Hui to his face—you acted like the statesmen of old.

sentences.zh: 朕退而歎息，方寄卿以腹心，何乃引去？」

translations.literal: After I withdrew I sighed; I had just entrusted you with my innermost confidence—why do you now withdraw?"
translations.idiomatic: I withdrew and sighed; I had just begun to trust you with my innermost counsels—why leave now?"

sentences.zh: 光曰：「臣與宰相爭論，不可留。」

translations.literal: Guang said: "Your servant has disputed with the chief minister and cannot remain."
translations.idiomatic: Guang replied, "I have quarreled openly with the chief minister—I cannot stay."

sentences.zh: 章九上，乃除資政殿學士、知紹興府，改提舉臨安府 洞霄宮。

translations.literal: After nine memorials he was appointed Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and prefect of Shaoxing, then changed to intendant of the Dongxiao Palace in Lin'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After nine memorials he was made Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and prefect of Shaoxing, then reassigned as intendant of the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 十一年冬，中丞万俟禼論光陰懷怨望，責授建寧軍節度副使，藤州安置。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year, Censor-in-Chief Moqi Xie accused Guang of secretly harboring resentment; he was demoted to Vice Military Commissioner of Jianning Army and settled at Teng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the eleventh year, Censor Moqi Xie charged him with brooding resentment; he was demoted to Vice Military Commissioner of Jianning and exiled to Teng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 越四年，移瓊州。

translations.literal: After four years he was transferred to Qiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he was moved to Qiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 居瓊州八年，仲子孟堅坐陸升之誣以私撰國史，獄成；

translations.literal: He dwelt at Qiong Prefecture eight years; his second son Mengjian was implicated by Lu Shengzhi's false charge of privately compiling a national history, and the case was concluded;
translations.idiomatic: After eight years on Qiong Island, his second son Mengjian was convicted on Lu Shengzhi's false charge of writing an unauthorized history;

sentences.zh: 呂願中又告光 與胡銓詩賦倡和，譏訕朝政，移昌化軍。

translations.literal: Lü Yuanzhong further reported that Guang had exchanged poems with Hu Quan, mocking court policy, and he was moved to Changhua Army.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yuanzhong then accused him of exchanging poems with Hu Quan that mocked the government, and he was banished farther to Changhua.

sentences.zh: 論文考史，怡然自適。

translations.literal: Discussing literature and examining history, he was content and at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to scholarship and history, serene in exile.

sentences.zh: 年逾八十，筆力精健。

translations.literal: Past eighty years of age, his brushwork remained vigorous and strong.
translations.idiomatic: Past eighty, his writing remained vigorous.

sentences.zh: 又三年，始以郊恩，復左朝奉大夫，任便居住。

translations.literal: After three more years, by grace of the suburban sacrifice amnesty he was restored to Left Grand Master for Court Audience and permitted to reside where he chose.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later an amnesty restored him to Left Grand Master for Court Audience with permission to live where he pleased.

sentences.zh: 至江州而卒。

translations.literal: He reached Jiang Prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Jiang Prefecture and died there.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，復資 政殿學士，賜諡莊簡。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong took the throne, he was posthumously restored as Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and given the posthumous title Zhuangjian (Solemn and Simple).
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong ascended the throne, Guang was posthumously restored as Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and given the posthumous title Zhuangjian (Solemn and Simple).

sentences.zh: 孟傳字文授，光幼子也。

translations.literal: Mengchuan, style name Wenshou, was Guang's youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: Mengchuan, styled Wenshou, was Guang's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 光南遷之日，才六歲。

translations.literal: On the day Guang was banished south, he was only six.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang was exiled south, the boy was only six.

sentences.zh: 以光遺表恩，累官至太府丞。

translations.literal: By grace of Guang's final memorial he rose through offices to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to his father's final petition he rose to Vice Director of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄願見之，孟傳曰：「行年六十，去計已決，不敢聞也。」

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou wished to see him; Mengchuan said: "I am sixty years old; my plan to leave office is already settled—I dare not hear of it."
translations.idiomatic: When Han Tuozhou asked to meet him, Mengchuan replied, "I am sixty and have already decided to retire—I will not answer such a summons."

sentences.zh: 由是出知江州。

translations.literal: Because of this he was sent out as prefect of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was posted out as prefect of Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以 朝請大夫、直寶謨閣致仕。

translations.literal: He retired as Grand Master for Court Audience and Direct Academician of the Hall of Treasured Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He retired with the titles Grand Master for Court Audience and Direct Academician of the Hall of Treasured Counsel.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty.

sentences.zh: 有《磐溪詩》二十卷，《文稿》三十卷，《宏辭類稿》十卷，《左氏說》十卷，《讀史》十卷，《雜志》十卷。

translations.literal: He had Panxi Poems in twenty juan, Draft Writings in thirty juan, Hongci Leigao in ten juan, Zuoshi Explanations in ten juan, Reading History in ten juan, and Miscellaneous Records in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: His works included Panxi Poems (20 juan), Draft Writings (30 juan), Hongci Leigao (10 juan), Zuoshi Explanations (10 juan), Reading History (10 juan), and Miscellaneous Records (10 juan).

sentences.zh: 博學多聞， 持身甚嚴，時推能世其家。

translations.literal: Broadly learned and well informed, he conducted himself with great strictness; contemporaries praised him as able to carry on the family tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Learned and rigorous in conduct, contemporaries hailed him as worthy to carry on his father's legacy.

sentences.zh: 許翰，字崧老，拱州襄邑人。

translations.literal: Xu Han, style name Songlao, was a man of Xiangyi in Gong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Han, styled Songlao, was a native of Xiangyi in Gong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 中元祐三年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Yuanyou.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi degree in the third year of the Yuanyou reign.

sentences.zh: 宣和七年，召為給事中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xuanhe he was summoned as Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xuanhe he was recalled as Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 為書抵時相，謂百姓困弊，起為盜賊，天下有危亡之憂。

translations.literal: He wrote to the chief minister, saying the people were exhausted and impoverished, rising as bandits, and the realm faced the worry of peril and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the chief minister warning that the people were destitute, turning to banditry, and the empire stood on the brink of collapse.

sentences.zh: 願罷雲中之師，修邊保境， 與民休息。

translations.literal: He wished to halt the army in Yunzhong, repair the borders and secure the territory, and let the people rest.
translations.idiomatic: He urged an end to the Yunzhong campaign, secure the frontier, and give the people respite.

sentences.zh: 高麗入貢，調民開運河，民間騷然。

translations.literal: When Goryeo sent tribute, the people were mobilized to open the transport canal and the countryside was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: When Goryeo sent tribute, the court conscripted labor to dredge the canal and the countryside erupted in protest.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人孫傅論高麗于國無功，不宜興大役，傅坐罷。

translations.literal: Drafting Secretary Sun Fu argued that Goryeo had rendered no service to the state and that great works should not be launched; Fu was dismissed on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting Secretary Sun Fu argued that Goryeo had done the state no good and that such grand projects were unwarranted; Sun was dismissed for his pains.

sentences.zh: 翰謂傅不當黜，時相怒，落職，提舉江州太平觀。

translations.literal: Han said Fu should not have been dismissed; the chief minister was angry, Han lost his post, and was made intendant of the Taiping Abbey in Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Han protested that Sun should not have been punished; the chief minister was furious, stripped Han of office, and sent him to oversee the Taiping Abbey in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，復以給事中召。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingkang he was again summoned as Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingkang era he was again summoned as Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 時金人攻京師甫退，翰造闕，即日賜對，除翰林學士，尋改御史中丞。

translations.literal: At the time the Jurchens had just withdrawn from attacking the capital; Han came to the palace, was granted audience the same day, appointed Hanlin Academician, and soon changed to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens had just lifted their siege of the capital; Han presented himself at court, was granted an audience that same day, made Hanlin Academician, and soon promoted to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 上疏言邊事，因陳決勝之策。

translations.literal: He memorialized on frontier affairs and set forth a strategy for decisive victory.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on frontier affairs and laid out a plan for victory.

sentences.zh: 陳邦昌為太宰，翰上疏力爭之。

translations.literal: When Chen Bangchang was made Grand Steward, Han memorialized forcefully against it.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Bangchang was named Grand Steward, Han submitted a fierce protest.

sentences.zh: 種 師道罷為中太一宮使，翰言：「師道名將，沉毅有謀，山西士卒，人人信服，不可使解兵柄。」

translations.literal: When Zhong Shidao was dismissed to become Commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace, Han said: "Shidao is a famous general, deep and resolute with stratagems; the soldiers of Shanxi all trust him—he must not be made to relinquish military authority."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong Shidao was demoted to palace commissioner, Han protested: "Shidao is a renowned general, steady and resourceful; the Shanxi troops trust him completely—do not strip him of command."

sentences.zh: 欽宗謂其老難用，翰曰：「秦始皇老王翦而用李信，兵辱于楚；

translations.literal: Qinzong said he was old and hard to employ; Han said: "Qin Shihuang considered Wang Jian too old and used Li Xin instead, and his army was shamed in Chu;
translations.idiomatic: Qinzong said the general was too old; Han replied, "Qin Shihuang thought Wang Jian too aged and sent the young Li Xin instead—and his army was humiliated in Chu;

sentences.zh: 漢宣 帝老趙充國，而卒能成金城之功。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Han considered Zhao Chongguo old, yet in the end he achieved the merit of the Golden City.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Han thought Zhao Chongguo too old, yet Zhao still won the Golden City campaign.

sentences.zh: 自呂望以來，用老將收功者，難一二數。

translations.literal: Since Lü Wang, cases of employing old generals to reap success are not easily counted on one or two fingers.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Duke of Zhou's day, victories won by veteran generals are too many to count on two hands.

sentences.zh: 以古揆今，師道雖老，可用也。」

translations.literal: Measuring the present by antiquity, though Shidao is old, he can be used."
translations.idiomatic: Judging by history, Shidao may be old, but he is still the man for the job."

sentences.zh: 且謂：「金人此行，存亡所系，令一大創，使失利去， 則中原可保，四夷可服。

translations.literal: He also said: "This Jurchen expedition concerns survival or destruction; if we inflict one great wound and make them withdraw in defeat, then the Central Plain can be preserved and the four barbarians can be brought to submission.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "This Jurchen campaign is a matter of life or death for the dynasty; one crushing blow that drives them off will preserve the Central Plain and awe the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 不然，將來再舉，必有不救之憂。

translations.literal: Otherwise, when they come again in the future, there will surely be the worry of what cannot be saved.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, when they return, the realm may face disaster beyond remedy.

sentences.zh: 宜起師道邀擊之。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to restore Shidao and have him intercept and strike them."
translations.idiomatic: He urged that Shidao be recalled to intercept and attack them."

sentences.zh: 上不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor would not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 擢中大夫、同知樞密院，論益不合，以病去，除延康殿學士、知亳州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; their views grew ever more at odds; he left on grounds of illness and was appointed Academic Gentleman of the Yankang Hall and prefect of Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Palace Attendant and made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, but his counsel increasingly clashed with the court's; pleading illness, he withdrew and was given the Yankang Hall academician title and made prefect of Bo.

sentences.zh: 坐 言者落職，提舉南京鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: On account of memorializing he lost his post and was made intendant of the Hongqing Palace in the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Denounced for his outspokenness, he was stripped of office and sent to oversee the Hongqing Palace at the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，召復端明殿學士、提舉萬壽觀，辭不至。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing he was summoned to restore his Duanming Hall academician rank and to intendant the Wanshou Abbey, but he declined and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxing he was recalled as Duanming Hall academician and intendant of Wanshou Abbey, but he refused the summons.

sentences.zh: 二月，復資政殿學士。

translations.literal: In the second month he was again made Zizheng Hall academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he was restored as Zizheng Hall academician.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，卒，贈光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the third year, fifth month, he died and was posthumously made Grand Mentor of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year he died and was posthumously made Grand Mentor of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 翰通經術，正直不撓，曆事三朝，致位政府，徒以黼、攸、潛善輩薰蕕異味，橫遭口語，志卒不展。

translations.literal: Han mastered the classics, was upright and unyielding, served three reigns and reached the highest government, yet only because Fu, You, Qianshan and their ilk were fragrant and foul in different measure he suffered slander unchecked and his ambitions never unfolded.
translations.idiomatic: Han was versed in the classics, upright and unbending; across three reigns he rose to the highest councils, yet Wang Fu, Cai You, Huang Qianshan, and men of their stripe—fragrant and foul mingled—set loose calumny against him, and his designs were never fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 綱雖力引之，不旋踵去，翰亦斥逐而死。

translations.literal: Though Gang vigorously recommended him, he left before turning his heel; Han too was driven out and died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang had pressed hard for his return, but Han withdrew almost at once; he too was hounded from office and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 所著書有《論語解》、《春秋傳》。

translations.literal: His writings include Explanations of the Analects and a Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: His works included Explanations of the Analects and a Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 許景衡

translations.literal: Xu Jingheng
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingheng

sentences.zh: 許景衡，字少伊，溫州里安人。

translations.literal: Xu Jingheng, style name Shaoyi, was a man of Li'an in Wen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingheng, styled Shaoyi, was a native of Li'an in Wen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 登元祐九年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the ninth year of Yuanyou.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi degree in the ninth year of the Yuanyou reign.

sentences.zh: 宣和六年，召為監察御史，遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xuanhe he was summoned as Investigating Censor and transferred to Attending Censor within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xuanhe he was recalled as Investigating Censor and soon promoted to Palace Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 是時，王黼、蔡攸用事，景衡言：「尚書省比闕長官，而同知樞 密院亦久闕。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Fu and Cai You were in power; Jingheng said: "The Department of State Affairs lately lacks a chief, and the Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs has also long been vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu and Cai You then held sway; Jingheng said, "The Department of State Affairs has gone too long without a chief minister, and the Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs has likewise stood empty.

sentences.zh: 雖三公通治三省，然文昌政事之本，樞密總兵之地，各有攸屬，安可久虛其位？

translations.literal: Though the Three Dukes may broadly administer all three departments, yet Wenchang is the root of civil government and the Bureau of Military Affairs the seat where armies are gathered—each has its proper domain; how can their posts be left vacant long?
translations.idiomatic: Though the Three Excellencies may nominally oversee all three departments, civil affairs have their foundation at Wenchang and military affairs at the Bureau of Military Affairs—each has its proper sphere; how can these posts stand empty for long?

sentences.zh: 願博采公議，遴選忠賢，以補政府之闕。」

translations.literal: I wish broadly to gather public opinion and select loyal worthies to fill the gaps in government."
translations.idiomatic: I urge that public counsel be gathered widely and loyal worthies chosen to fill the vacancies at court."

sentences.zh: 遂大忤黼意。

translations.literal: This greatly offended Fu's mind.
translations.idiomatic: This deeply enraged Wang Fu.

sentences.zh: 朝廷用童貫為 河東、北宣撫使，將北伐，景衡論其貪繆不可用者數十事，不報。

translations.literal: The court employed Tong Guan as Commissioner for Pacification of Hedong and Hebei and was about to launch a northern expedition; Jingheng set forth dozens of matters showing his greed and folly and that he could not be used, but there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Tong Guan Commissioner for Pacification of Hedong and Hebei in preparation for a northern campaign; Jingheng listed dozens of reasons why his greed and incompetence disqualified him—but no reply came.

sentences.zh: 睦寇平，江、浙郡縣殘毀，而茶鹽比較之法如故。

translations.literal: When the Muzhou rebels were pacified, the commanderies and counties of Jiang and Zhe were ravaged, yet the tea-and-salt comparative-assessment law remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: After the Fang La rebellion was put down, Jiang and Zhe prefectures lay in ruins, yet the tea-and-salt quota comparison system remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 景衡奏：「茶鹽之法，當以食之眾寡為歲額之高下。

translations.literal: Jingheng memorialized: "The tea-and-salt law ought to take the multitude or fewness of consumers as the basis for raising or lowering the annual quota.
translations.idiomatic: Jingheng submitted: "Tea-and-salt levies ought to rise and fall with the number of consumers.

sentences.zh: 今收復之後，戶版半耗，民力蕭然，而茶鹽比較不減於昔。

translations.literal: Now after recovery household registers are half depleted, the people's strength is desolate, yet tea-and-salt comparative assessment is not reduced from before.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the region has been recovered, household registers are half empty and the people exhausted, yet the comparative quotas are no lower than before.

sentences.zh: 民欲無困得乎？」

translations.literal: Can the people hope not to be distressed?"
translations.idiomatic: How can the people escape distress?"

sentences.zh: 奏上，詔兩浙、江東路權免茶鹽比較，賊平日仍舊。

translations.literal: When the memorial was sent up, an edict temporarily exempted the Two Zhes and Jiangdong circuits from tea-and-salt comparative assessment; on ordinary days of banditry it would remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached the throne; an edict temporarily suspended tea-and-salt comparisons in the Two Zhes and Jiangdong circuits, to resume only when banditry had fully subsided.

sentences.zh: 朝廷既興燕雲之師，調度不繼，誅求益急。

translations.literal: Once the court had raised armies for Yan-Yun, supplies could not keep pace and exactions grew ever more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: After the court launched the Yan-Yun campaign, logistics faltered and exactions grew ever harsher.

sentences.zh: 景衡奏：「財力匱乏在節用，民力困弊在恤民。

translations.literal: Jingheng memorialized: "When fiscal strength is exhausted the remedy lies in economizing; when the people's strength is worn out the remedy lies in cherishing the people.
translations.idiomatic: Jingheng wrote: "Fiscal exhaustion demands frugality; popular exhaustion demands compassion.

sentences.zh: 今不急之務。

translations.literal: Now are affairs not urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet non-urgent spending abounds.

sentences.zh: 若營繕諸役，花石綱運，其名不一。

translations.literal: Such as various repair corvées, Huashi Convoy transport—their names are not one.
translations.idiomatic: Palace repairs, the Huashi Convoy, and the like go under countless names.
