sentences.zh: 吏員猥多，軍額冗 濫。

translations.literal: Administrative personnel are excessively numerous; military rolls are bloated and excessive.
translations.idiomatic: The civil bureaucracy is swollen and military rolls padded beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 又無名功賞，非常賜予，皆夤緣僥倖，幹請無厭，宜節以祖宗之制而省去之。」

translations.literal: Moreover unnamed merit rewards and extraordinary grants all climb by connections and luck, importuning without satiety—they ought to be restrained by ancestral institutions and cut away."
translations.idiomatic: Unmerited rewards and extraordinary favors are seized through patronage and chance, with endless requests—cut them back to fit the ancestral statutes."

sentences.zh: 且極論和買、和糴、鹽法之害，不報。

translations.literal: He also argued to the limit the harm of harmonized purchase, harmonized grain collection, and salt laws; no response.
translations.idiomatic: He also laid bare the harm of compulsory purchase, state grain levy, and the salt monopoly—and again received no answer.

sentences.zh: 會知洋州吳岩夫以私書抵執政子，道景衡 之賢。

translations.literal: It happened that Wu Yanfu, prefect of Yang Prefecture, sent a private letter to a chief minister's son praising Jingheng's worth.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wu Yanfu, prefect of Yang, wrote privately to a chief minister's son praising Jingheng's talents.

sentences.zh: 因從子婿符寶郎周離亨以達，離亨繆以其書誤致王黼，黼用是中景衡，逐之。

translations.literal: It passed through his nephew-by-marriage, Talisman Keeping Gentleman Zhou Liheng, to reach them; Liheng mistakenly sent the letter to Wang Fu, and Fu used this to strike at Jingheng and drove him out.
translations.idiomatic: It was forwarded through his nephew-in-law Zhou Liheng, Keeper of the Talismans—but Liheng mistakenly delivered it to Wang Fu, who seized on the incident to ruin Jingheng and had him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 欽宗即位，以左正言召，旋改太常少卿兼太子諭德，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Qinzong took the throne he was summoned as Left Remonstrator, soon changed to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices concurrent with Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and transferred to Drafting Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinzong ascended the throne Jingheng was summoned as Left Remonstrator, soon made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and concurrent Tutor of the Heir Apparent, then promoted to Drafting Secretary.

sentences.zh: 侍御史李光、正言程瑀以鯁亮忤執政斥，景衡為辨白，坐落職予祠。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Li Guang and Remonstrator Cheng Yu were forthright and bright, offended the chief ministers and were expelled; Jingheng spoke in their defense, lost his post and was granted a temple stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Li Guang and Remonstrator Cheng Yu, bold and upright, had offended the chief ministers and been driven out; Jingheng defended them, was stripped of office, and given a temple sinecure.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，以給事中召，既至，除御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne he was summoned as Supervising Secretary; once he arrived he was made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong came to the throne Jingheng was recalled as Supervising Secretary and, on arrival, made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 宗澤為東京留守，言者附黃潛善等，多攻其短，欲逐去之。

translations.literal: Zong Ze was Eastern Capital regent; memorialists attached to Huang Qianshan and others attacked his faults at length, wishing to drive him away.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ze served as regent of the Eastern Capital; critics aligned with Huang Qianshan and his faction piled on his faults, seeking his removal.

sentences.zh: 景衡奏曰：「臣自浙渡淮，以至行在。

translations.literal: Jingheng memorialized: "Your servant from Zhe crossed the Huai to the Mobile Court.
translations.idiomatic: Jingheng wrote: "Since I crossed the Huai from Zhe to reach the Mobile Court,

sentences.zh: 聞澤之為尹，威 名政事，卓然過人，雖不識其人，竊用歎慕。

translations.literal: Hearing of Ze as magistrate, his aweful name and governance plainly surpass others—though I do not know the man, I privately sigh and admire.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard of Ze's tenure—his renown and governance plainly surpass all others; though I have never met him, I cannot but admire him from afar.

sentences.zh: 臣以為去冬京城內，有赤心為國如澤等數輩，其禍變未至如是之酷。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that last winter within the capital, if there had been several men with loyal hearts for the state like Ze, the calamity and upheaval would not have reached such cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Had loyal men like Ze stood in the capital last winter, the catastrophe might never have grown so cruel.

sentences.zh: 今若較其小短，不顧盡忠徇國之節，則不恕已甚。

translations.literal: Now if one compares his small faults and ignores his integrity of giving full loyalty and dying for the state, then lack of forgiveness has gone too far.
translations.idiomatic: To harp on petty faults and ignore his devotion to the realm would be wanton cruelty.

sentences.zh: 且開封宗廟社稷所在，苟欲罷澤，別遣留守，不識搢紳中威名政事有加於澤者乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover Kaifeng is where the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain stand; if one wishes to dismiss Ze and separately dispatch another regent, does one not know any gentry in whom aweful name and governance surpass Ze?"
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng holds the imperial tombs and altars; if Ze is removed, is there any among the court officials whose renown and governance exceed his?"

sentences.zh: 疏入，上大悟，封以示澤，澤乃安。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor greatly understood, sealed it and showed it to Ze, and Ze was thereby reassured.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached the emperor, who was deeply moved, sealed it and sent it to Ze, who was thereby reassured.

sentences.zh: 杭州叛卒陳通作亂，權浙西提刑趙叔近招降之，請授以官。

translations.literal: The Hangzhou mutineer Chen Tong raised disorder; acting Zhexi Judicial Intendant Zhao Shujin recruited his surrender and requested he be granted office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hangzhou mutineer Chen Tong rebelled, Acting Zhexi Judicial Intendant Zhao Shujin induced his surrender and asked that he be given an official post.

sentences.zh: 景衡曰：「官吏無罪而受誅。

translations.literal: Jingheng said: "Officials were guiltless yet received execution.
translations.idiomatic: Jingheng said, "Innocent officials were put to death,

sentences.zh: 叛卒有罪而蒙賞，賞罰倒置，莫此為甚。」

translations.literal: Mutineers had guilt yet received reward—rewards and punishments inverted, nothing surpasses this."
translations.idiomatic: while guilty mutineers are rewarded—never was reward and punishment so perverted."

sentences.zh: 卒奏罷之。

translations.literal: In the end he memorialized and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized against it and the appointment was halted.

sentences.zh: 除尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 有 大政事，必請間極論。

translations.literal: When there were great state affairs he invariably requested private audience to argue to the limit.
translations.idiomatic: On weighty matters of state he always sought a private audience to speak his mind fully.

sentences.zh: 潛善、伯彥以景衡異己，共排沮之。

translations.literal: Qianshan and Boyan, because Jingheng differed from them, together blocked and thwarted him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan, seeing Jingheng as an opponent, combined to thwart him at every turn.

sentences.zh: 或言正、二月之交，乃太一正遷之日，宜於禁中設壇望拜。

translations.literal: Someone said that at the junction of the first and second months was the day of the Great Unity's proper migration, and it was fitting to set an altar in the Forbidden precinct and look toward it in worship.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged that at the turn of the first and second months—the day when the Great Unity star shifted position—the palace should erect an altar and worship it.

sentences.zh: 高宗以問景衡，曰：「修德愛民，天自降福， 何迎拜太一之有？」

translations.literal: Gaozong asked Jingheng; he said: "Cultivate virtue and cherish the people, Heaven itself will send blessings—why welcome and worship the Great Unity?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong asked Jingheng, who replied, "Cultivate virtue and love the people, and Heaven sends blessing of its own—why bow to the Great Unity star?"

sentences.zh: 初，李綱議建都，以關中為上，南陽次之，建康為下。

translations.literal: At first Li Gang debated establishing the capital, ranking Guanzhong first, Nanyang second, and Jianye last.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Li Gang ranked capitals: Guanzhong first, Nanyang second, Jianye last.

sentences.zh: 綱既相，遂主南陽之議。

translations.literal: Once Gang became chief minister he then upheld the Nanyang plan.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office, he pressed for Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 景衡為中丞，奏：「南陽無險阻，且密邇盜賊，漕運不繼，不若建康天險可據， 請定計巡幸。」

translations.literal: Jingheng as Censor-in-Chief memorialized: "Nanyang has no strategic barriers and lies close to bandits; grain transport by canal cannot be sustained—better Jianye, where heaven's barriers may be held; I request a fixed plan for the imperial progress."
translations.idiomatic: As Censor-in-Chief, Jingheng wrote: "Nanyang has no natural defenses, lies too close to bandit country, and cannot sustain canal supply—Jianye's terrain is far stronger; I urge a settled plan to move the court there."

sentences.zh: 潛善等傾綱使去，南陽之議遂格。

translations.literal: Qianshan and others overthrew Gang and made him leave, and the Nanyang plan was then blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Qianshan and his allies ousted Li Gang, and the Nanyang plan died.

sentences.zh: 至是，諜報金人攻河陽、汜水，景衡又奏請南幸建康。

translations.literal: At this time spies reported Jurchens attacking Heyang and Sishui; Jingheng again memorialized requesting the southward progress to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Then scouts reported Jurchen attacks on Heyang and Sishui, and Jingheng again urged a southern move to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 已而有詔還京，罷景衡為資政殿大學士、提舉杭州洞霄宮。

translations.literal: Before long there was an edict to return to the capital; Jingheng was dismissed to Zizheng Hall Grand Academician and intendant of the Dongxiao Abbey in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered the court back to the capital; Jingheng was demoted to Zizheng Hall Grand Academician and sent to oversee the Dongxiao Abbey in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 至瓜洲，得暍疾，及京口卒，年五十七，諡忠簡。

translations.literal: Reaching Guazhou he contracted heatstroke; at Jingkou he died, age fifty-seven, posthumous name Zhongjian.
translations.idiomatic: At Guazhou he was stricken with heatstroke; he died at Jingkou, aged fifty-seven, and was posthumously titled Loyal and Simple.

sentences.zh: 景衡得程頤之學，志慮忠純，議論不與時俯仰。

translations.literal: Jingheng obtained Cheng Yi's learning; his aims and thoughts were loyal and pure, his discourse not bending with the age.
translations.idiomatic: Jingheng studied under Cheng Yi; his intent was loyal and pure, and he would not trim his counsel to the fashion of the day.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，李綱議幸南陽，宗澤請還京，景衡乃請幸建康。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyan Li Gang debated proceeding to Nanyang, Zong Ze requested returning to the capital, and Jingheng then requested proceeding to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyan Li Gang favored Nanyang, Zong Ze urged a return to the capital, and Jingheng pressed for Jianye.

sentences.zh: 黃潛善等素惡其異己，暨車駕駐揚州，怵于傳聞，不得 已下還京之詔，遂借渡江之議罪之，斥逐而死。

translations.literal: Huang Qianshan and others had long hated his differing from them; once the imperial carriage halted at Yangzhou, alarmed by rumors, they had no choice but to issue the edict to return to the capital, then used the plan of crossing the river as a crime against him, drove him out and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Qianshan and his faction had long resented his independence; when the court paused at Yangzhou, frightened by rumor, they reluctantly issued the edict to return north—then seized on his counsel to cross the Yangzi as a pretext to purge him, and he died in exile.

sentences.zh: 既沒，高宗思之曰：「朕自即位以來，執政忠直，遇事敢言，惟許景衡。」

translations.literal: After his death Gaozong thought of him and said: "Since I took the throne, among those in government who were loyal and straight, on affairs daring to speak—only Xu Jingheng."
translations.idiomatic: After his death Gaozong mused, "Since my enthronement, of all who served loyally and spoke boldly on the affairs of state, only Xu Jingheng."

sentences.zh: 詔賜景衡家溫州官舍一區。

translations.literal: An edict granted Jingheng's household one government residence district in Wen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a government residence in Wenzhou granted to Jingheng's family.

sentences.zh: 張愨，字誠伯，河間樂壽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Que, style name Chengbo, was a man of Lesou in Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Que, styled Chengbo, was a native of Lesou in Hejian.

sentences.zh: 登元祐六年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the sixth year of Yuanyou.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in the sixth year of the Yuanyou reign.

sentences.zh: 累遷龍圖閣學士、計度都轉運使。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he became Longtu Pavilion academician and Director of Aggregate Transport Commissaries.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through promotion to Longtu Pavilion academician and Director of Aggregate Transport Commissaries.

sentences.zh: 高宗為兵馬大元帥，募諸道兵勤王，愨飛輓踵道，建議即元帥府印給鹽鈔， 以便商旅。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was Grand Marshal of Horse and Foot he gathered troops from all circuits to rescue the throne; Que rushed transport so that wheels followed wheels along the road, and proposed that the marshal's office immediately stamp and issue salt certificates to facilitate merchants and travelers.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong was Grand Marshal rallying troops from every circuit, Que drove supply wagons in an unbroken stream and proposed that the marshal's office issue salt certificates on the spot to keep commerce moving.

sentences.zh: 不閱旬，得緡錢五十萬以佐軍。

translations.literal: Within less than ten days he obtained five hundred thousand strings of cash to assist the army.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he raised five hundred thousand strings of cash for the war chest.

sentences.zh: 高宗器重之，命以便宜權大名尹兼北京留守、馬步軍都總管。

translations.literal: Gaozong greatly valued him and ordered him at discretion to act as acting Prefect of Daming concurrent Northern Capital regent and Grand Commander of all Horse and Foot.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong relied on him heavily and gave him discretionary authority as acting Prefect of Daming, Northern Capital regent, and Grand Commander of Horse and Foot.

sentences.zh: 愨初聞二帝北行，率副總管顏岐等三上箋勸進。

translations.literal: When Que first heard the two emperors had gone north, he led Deputy Commander Yan Qi and others to submit three memorials urging enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: When Que first learned the two emperors had been carried north, he led Deputy Commander Yan Qi and others in submitting three memorials urging Gaozong to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 最後，愨上 書，極論中原不可一日無君，高宗為之感悟。

translations.literal: Finally Que submitted a letter arguing to the limit that the Central Plain could not go one day without a sovereign; Gaozong was moved by it to understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Finally Que wrote at length that the Central Plain could not endure a single day without an emperor—and Gaozong was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 建炎改元，為戶部尚書，除同知樞密院事、措置戶部財用兼御營副使。

translations.literal: When the Jianyan reign was proclaimed he was Minister of Revenue, appointed Vice Commissioner of Bureau of Military Affairs, Commissioner for Arranging Ministry of Revenue Finances concurrent Vice Commissioner of the Imperial Camp.
translations.idiomatic: With the Jianyan reign he became Minister of Revenue, then Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, commissioner for fiscal arrangements, and deputy commissioner of the Imperial Camp.

sentences.zh: 建言：「三河之民。

translations.literal: He offered counsel: "The people of the Three Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed: "The people of the Three Rivers—

sentences.zh: 怨敵深入骨髓，恨不殲殄其類，以報國家之仇。

translations.literal: Hatred of the enemy penetrates to the marrow; they regret not exterminating their kind to repay the state's enmity.
translations.idiomatic: bear hatred for the foe to the bone and long to annihilate them to avenge the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 請依唐人澤潞步兵、 雄邊子弟遺意，募民聯以什伍，而寓兵于農，使合力抗敵，謂之巡社。」

translations.literal: I request following the Tang intent of Zelu foot soldiers and Xiongbian frontier sons, recruiting the people linked in tens and fives, while lodging troops within farming, to make them combine strength to resist the enemy—called Xunshe."
translations.idiomatic: Following the Tang examples of the Zelu foot soldiers and the frontier militia of the Xiongbian, I propose organizing the people in tens and fives, soldiers nested among farmers, jointly resisting the enemy—called Patrol Communities."

sentences.zh: 為法精詳，前此論民兵者莫及也。

translations.literal: The regulations were meticulous in detail; none who had discussed militia before could match it.
translations.idiomatic: His regulations were so thorough that no earlier militia plan could equal them.

sentences.zh: 詔集為書行之。

translations.literal: An edict gathered it into a book and enacted it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered them compiled into a handbook and put into practice.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左丞，官至中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; his highest office reached Secretariat Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and eventually reached Secretariat Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 愨善理財，論錢谷利害，猶指諸掌。

translations.literal: Que was skilled at managing finances; discussing the profit and harm of monetary grain affairs was like pointing at his palm.
translations.idiomatic: Que excelled at finance; on revenue and grain he spoke as if reading from his palm.

sentences.zh: 在朝諤諤有大臣節，然論議可否，不形辭色，未嘗失同列之歡。

translations.literal: In court he was upright with the integrity of a great minister, yet in debate of approval or rejection he did not show it in words or countenance, and never lost his peers' goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: In council he was forthright and possessed a great minister's bearing, yet on matters of dispute he showed neither face nor temper, and never lost the goodwill of his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡忠穆。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous name Zhongmu.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Loyal and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 上每念之，謂愨謀國盡忠，遇事敢諫，古之遺直也。

translations.literal: The emperor often thought of him, saying Que in planning the state gave full loyalty, on affairs dared to remonstrate—a straight man of antiquity left behind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often recalled him, saying Que served the realm with complete loyalty and dared speak bluntly on public affairs—an upright man in the mold of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 張所，青州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Suo was a man of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Suo was a native of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，曆官為監察御史。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi and through offices became Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi degree and rose to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，遣所按視陵寢，還，上疏言：「河東、河北，天下之根本。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne he sent Suo to inspect the imperial tombs; returning, he submitted a memorial saying: "Hedong and Hebei are the root of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On Gaozong's enthronement Suo was sent to inspect the imperial tombs; on his return he memorialized: "Hedong and Hebei are the empire's foundation.

sentences.zh: 昨者誤用奸臣之謀，始割三鎮，繼割兩河， 其民怨入骨髓，至今無不扼腕。

translations.literal: Yesterday the court wrongly used treacherous ministers' schemes, first ceding the Three Prefectures, then ceding the Two Rivers—their people's resentment entered the marrow, and to this day none do not wring their wrists.
translations.idiomatic: Misguided ministers led us first to cede the Three Prefectures, then the Two Rivers; the people there resent it to the marrow, and every hand still clenches in grief.

sentences.zh: 若因而用之，則可藉以守；

translations.literal: If by this means they are employed, then one may rely on them to defend;
translations.idiomatic: If we rally them now, they can hold the north for us;

sentences.zh: 不則兩河兵民，無所系望，陛下之事去矣。」

translations.literal: otherwise the armies and people of the Two Rivers have nothing to which to attach their hopes, and Your Majesty's enterprise is lost."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise the soldiers and people of the Two Rivers will lose all hope, and Your Majesty's cause is lost."

sentences.zh: 且論還京師有五利，謂國之安危，在乎兵之強弱、將相之賢 不肖，不在乎都之遷不遷。

translations.literal: He also discussed five benefits of returning to the capital, saying the state's safety or peril lies in whether armies are strong or weak and whether generals and ministers are worthy or not, not in whether the capital is moved or not moved.
translations.idiomatic: He also laid out five advantages of returning to the capital, arguing that a realm's fate depends on the strength of its armies and the quality of its generals and ministers—not on where the court sits.

sentences.zh: 又條上兩河利害。

translations.literal: He also itemized and submitted the profit and harm of the Two Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a detailed account of the Two Rivers' strategic interests.

sentences.zh: 上欲以其事付所，會所言黃潛善奸邪不可用，恐害新政。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to entrust these affairs to Suo, but it happened that he spoke of Huang Qianshan as treacherous and evil and unusable, fearing harm to the new administration.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to entrust the affair to Suo, but Suo had denounced Huang Qianshan as treacherous and unfit for office, which might sabotage the new government.

sentences.zh: 乃罷所御史，改兵部郎中。

translations.literal: Thereupon Suo was dismissed from the censorate and changed to Bureau Secretary in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Suo was therefore removed from the censorate and made a bureau secretary in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 尋責所鳳州團練副使，江州安置。

translations.literal: Soon Suo was demoted to Regiment Vice Commander of Feng Prefecture and settled at Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was demoted to Regiment Vice Commander of Fengzhou and exiled to Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 後李綱入相，欲薦所經略兩河，以其嘗言潛善故，難之。

translations.literal: Later when Li Gang entered as chief minister he wished to recommend Suo to oversee the Two Rivers, but because Suo had once spoken against Qianshan it was difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Li Gang became chief minister, he wanted to appoint Suo to oversee the Two Rivers but hesitated because Suo had once denounced Huang Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 一日，與潛善從容言曰：「今河北未有人，獨一張所可用，又以狂言抵罪。

translations.literal: One day he said to Qianshan in an easy manner: "Now in Hebei there is no one; only one Zhang Suo can be used, and yet for wild words he has been punished.
translations.idiomatic: One day he spoke to Huang Qianshan at ease: "Hebei has no capable man left but Zhang Suo—and he languishes in exile for blunt words.

sentences.zh: 不得已抆拭用之，使為招 撫，冒死立功以贖過，不亦善乎？」

translations.literal: Having no choice but to wipe and use him, let him serve as pacification commissioner, risking death to achieve merit and redeem his fault—is this not good?"
translations.idiomatic: We have no choice but to wipe the slate clean and send him as pacification commissioner to risk his life for merit and redeem his fault—would that not serve us well?"

sentences.zh: 潛善許諾，乃借所直龍圖閣，充河北招撫使。

translations.literal: Qianshan promised; thereupon Suo was lent the post of Direct Dragon Diagram Pavilion academician and made Hebei Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Qianshan agreed; Suo was lent the title Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion and made Hebei Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 賜內府錢百萬緡，給空名告千餘道；

translations.literal: He was granted a million strings of cash from the inner treasury and given over a thousand blank commission documents;
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a million strings from the inner treasury and more than a thousand blank commission notices;

sentences.zh: 以京西卒三千為衛，將佐官屬，許自辟置，一 切以便宜從事。

translations.literal: three thousand soldiers of the Western Capital circuit as guard, with generals, assistants, officials and staff—permitted to select and appoint on his own, entirely to act as discretion required.
translations.idiomatic: three thousand Western Capital troops as his escort, with authority to appoint his own staff and act entirely at his discretion.

sentences.zh: 所入見，條上利害。

translations.literal: Suo on entering audience itemized and submitted profit and harm.
translations.idiomatic: On audience Zhang Suo laid out the strategic advantages and risks point by point.

sentences.zh: 上賜五品服遣行，命直秘閣王圭為宣撫司參謀官佐之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted fifth-rank court robes and sent him on his way, ordering Direct Secretariat Pavilion Wang Gui as Pacification Commission planning officer to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bestowed fifth-rank robes and dispatched him, appointing Wang Gui of the Direct Secretariat Pavilion as planning officer on the Pacification Commission to assist him.

sentences.zh: 河北轉運副使張益謙附黃潛善意，奏所置司北京非是；

translations.literal: Hebei transport vice commissioner Zhang Yiqian attached to Huang Qianshan's intent and memorialized that establishing the commission at the Northern Capital was wrong;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yiqian, vice commissioner of Hebei transport, sided with Huang Qianshan and memorialized that the commission should not have been set up at the Northern Capital;

sentences.zh: 且言自置招撫，河北盜賊愈熾，不若罷之，專以其事付帥司。

translations.literal: and said that since pacification was established, Hebei bandits grew fiercer—better to abolish it and entrust the affair solely to the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: and argued that banditry in Hebei had only worsened since the pacification office was created; it would be better to abolish it and leave the matter entirely to the military command.

sentences.zh: 李綱言：「張所今留京師，招集將佐，尚未 及行，益謙何以知其擾？

translations.literal: Li Gang said: "Zhang Suo now stays at the capital gathering generals and staff and has not yet gone on his mission—how does Yiqian know he is causing disturbance?
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang said, "Zhang Suo is still in the capital recruiting officers and has not yet departed—how can Yiqian already know he is causing trouble?

sentences.zh: 朝廷以河北民無所歸，聚而為盜，故置司招撫，因其力而用之，豈由置司乃有盜賊乎？

translations.literal: The court, because Hebei people had nowhere to turn and gathered as bandits, therefore established a pacification commission to use their strength—how could establishing the commission create bandits?
translations.idiomatic: The court set up the pacification commission because displaced people in Hebei had nowhere to go and turned to banditry, so that their strength might be turned to the state's use—how could the commission itself have created the bandits?

sentences.zh: 今京東、西群盜公行，攻掠郡縣，亦豈招撫司過耶？

translations.literal: Now in the Eastern and Western Capital circuits bandits openly roam, attacking and plundering prefectures and counties—is that also the pacification commission's fault?
translations.idiomatic: Bandits now roam openly through the Eastern and Western Capital circuits, raiding prefectures and counties—surely that is not the pacification commission's fault either?

sentences.zh: 時方艱危，朝廷欲有所經理，益謙小臣，乃以非理沮抑，此必有使之者。」

translations.literal: Times are perilous and the court wishes to manage affairs; Yiqian is a petty official yet unreasonably obstructs—there must be someone directing him."
translations.idiomatic: The realm is in grave peril and the court is trying to set things right; Yiqian is a minor official, yet he obstructs us without cause—someone must be putting him up to it."

sentences.zh: 上乃命益謙分析，命下樞密院，汪伯彥猶用其奏詰責招撫司。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Yiqian to explain himself; the order went to the Bureau of Military Affairs, yet Wang Boyan still used his memorial to reproach the pacification commission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yiqian to submit a written explanation and sent the matter to the Bureau of Military Affairs, but Wang Boyan still used Yiqian's memorial to rebuke the pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 李綱與伯彥爭于上前，伯彥 語塞。

translations.literal: Li Gang and Boyan argued before the emperor; Boyan was left speechless.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gang and Wang Boyan disputed the matter before the throne, and Boyan had no reply.

sentences.zh: 所方招來豪傑，以王彥為都統制，岳飛為準備將，而李綱已罷相。

translations.literal: Suo was just recruiting heroes, making Wang Yan overall commander and Yue Fei preparation general, but Li Gang had already been dismissed as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Suo was just recruiting bold men, appointing Wang Yan overall commander and Yue Fei preparation general, when Li Gang was already removed from the chief ministership.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以王圭代之，所落直龍圖閣，嶺南安置。

translations.literal: The court replaced him with Wang Gui; Suo was stripped of Direct Dragon Diagram Pavilion and settled in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: The court replaced him with Wang Gui; Suo lost his Direct Dragon Diagram Pavilion title and was exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 卒於貶所。

translations.literal: He died at his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: He died in exile.

sentences.zh: 子宗本，以岳飛奏補官。

translations.literal: His son Zongben received an official appointment through Yue Fei's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongben was given office on Yue Fei's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 陳禾，字秀實，明州鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Chen He, style Xiushi, a native of Yin County in Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen He, courtesy name Xiushi, was from Yin County in Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉元符三年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Yuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: He earned the jinshi degree in 1100, the third year of Yuanfu.

sentences.zh: 累遷辟雍博士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 時方以傳注記問為學，禾始崇尚義理，黜抑浮華。

translations.literal: At the time learning took commentary and textual questioning as its model; He first upheld principle and meaning and suppressed empty show.
translations.idiomatic: Scholarship then prized glosses and rote interrogation; He was among the first to champion moral principle and to reject mere ornament.

sentences.zh: 入對契旨，擢監察御史、殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: On entering audience he matched the emperor's intent and was elevated to investigating censor and palace attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: In audience he pleased the throne and was promoted to investigating censor and then palace censor.

sentences.zh: 蔡京遣酷使李孝壽窮治章綖鑄錢獄，連及士大夫甚眾，禾奏免孝壽。

translations.literal: Cai Jing sent harsh envoy Li Xiaoshou to pursue to the end the Zhang Sui coin-casting case, implicating very many scholar-officials; He memorialized to dismiss Xiaoshou.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing dispatched the ruthless Li Xiaoshou to prosecute the Zhang Sui counterfeiting case to the end, sweeping up a host of gentlemen; He memorialized for Xiaoshou's removal.

sentences.zh: 京子壝為太常少卿，何執中婿蔡芝為將作監，皆疏其罪，罷之。

translations.literal: Jing's son Huang was Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, He Zhizhong's son-in-law Cai Zhi was Director of Palace Construction—all had their crimes detailed and were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He exposed and secured the dismissal of Cai Jing's son Huang as Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Shrine and of He Zhizhong's son-in-law Cai Zhi as Director of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 天下久平，武備寬弛，東南尤甚。

translations.literal: The realm had long been at peace, military preparedness lax and slack, especially in the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Long peace had left the empire's defenses slack, nowhere more so than in the southeast.

sentences.zh: 禾請增戍、繕城壁，以戒不虞。

translations.literal: He requested increased garrisons and repair of city walls to guard against the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: He urged stronger garrisons and repairs to the walls against unforeseen danger.

sentences.zh: 或指為生事，格不下。

translations.literal: Some called it making trouble; the proposal was blocked and not enacted.
translations.idiomatic: Critics charged him with stirring trouble, and the memorial was shelved.

sentences.zh: 其後盜起，人服其先見。

translations.literal: Afterwards bandits arose and people admired his foresight.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits later rose, many marveled at his foresight.

sentences.zh: 遷左正言，俄除給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Rectifier and shortly after made Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Left Rectifier and soon appointed Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 時童貫權益張，與黃經臣胥用事，御史中丞盧航表裏為奸，搢紳側目。

translations.literal: At the time Tong Guan's power grew daily; with Huang Jingchen he jointly wielded affairs, Vice Censor-in-Chief Lu Hang outside and inside as villain—the gentry glared sideways.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guan's influence was swelling; he and Huang Jingchen ran the government together while Censor-in-Chief Lu Hang abetted them from within—court gentlemen watched in alarm.

sentences.zh: 禾曰：「此國家安危之本也。

translations.literal: He said: "This is the root of the state's safety and peril.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "This strikes at the very root of the state's safety.

sentences.zh: 吾位言責，此而不言，一遷給舍，則非其職矣。」

translations.literal: I hold the office of speaking responsibility; on this not to speak—once transferred to supervising secretary, it would no longer be my duty."
translations.idiomatic: My office is to speak out. If I stay silent on this now, once I become supervising secretary I will no longer be charged with such remonstrance."

sentences.zh: 未拜命， 首抗疏劾貫。

translations.literal: Before receiving his appointment he first submitted a confronting memorial impeaching Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Before even accepting the new post, he led with a bold memorial impeaching Tong Guan.

sentences.zh: 復劾經臣：「怙寵弄權，誇炫朝列。

translations.literal: He again impeached Jingchen: "Relying on favor to manipulate power, boasting before the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Huang Jingchen: "He leans on imperial favor to play with power and struts before the court.

sentences.zh: 每云詔令皆出其手，言上將用某人，舉某事，已而詔下，悉如其言。

translations.literal: He always says edicts all issue from his hand; saying the emperor will use a certain man or undertake a certain affair, and when the edict comes down it all matches his words.
translations.idiomatic: He brags that every edict passes through his hands, predicts whom the emperor will appoint or what he will decree, and when the order appears it matches his boast to the letter.

sentences.zh: 夫發號施令，國之重事，黜幽陟明，天子大 權，奈何使宦寺得與？

translations.literal: Issuing orders and carrying out commands are grave affairs of state; dismissing the obscure and advancing the bright are the Son of Heaven's great powers—how can eunuch attendants be allowed a share?
translations.idiomatic: To proclaim commands and wield the great power of appointing and dismissing is the emperor's alone—why should palace eunuchs have any part in it?

sentences.zh: 臣之所憂，不獨經臣，此塗一開，類進者眾，國家之禍，有不可遏，願亟竄之遠方。」

translations.literal: What your servant fears is not only Jingchen; once this path is opened, those who advance by kind will be many—the state's disaster may be unstoppable; I wish urgently to exile him to a distant region."
translations.idiomatic: My worry is not Huang Jingchen alone. Open this door and imitators will crowd in; the state's ruin may prove unstoppable. Exile him at once to the far marches."

sentences.zh: 論奏未終，上拂衣起。

translations.literal: The discussion and memorial were not finished when the emperor brushed his robe and rose.
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished, the emperor rose and turned away.

sentences.zh: 禾引上衣，請畢其說。

translations.literal: He pulled the emperor's upper robe and asked to complete his statement.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the emperor's robe and begged leave to finish.

sentences.zh: 衣裾落，上曰：「正言碎朕衣矣。」

translations.literal: The robe's hem fell away; the emperor said: "Rectifier, you have torn Our robe."
translations.idiomatic: The hem tore away. The emperor said, "Rectifier, you have torn Our robe."

sentences.zh: 禾言：「陛下不惜碎衣，臣豈惜碎首以報陛下？

translations.literal: He said: "Your Majesty does not spare a torn robe—how would your servant spare a shattered head to repay Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "If Your Majesty does not value a torn robe, how could your servant value his own life in answering you?

sentences.zh: 此曹今日受富貴之利，陛下他 日受危亡之禍。」

translations.literal: These fellows today receive the profit of wealth and rank; Your Majesty another day will receive the disaster of peril and ruin."
translations.idiomatic: They gain wealth and power today; Your Majesty will face ruin tomorrow."

sentences.zh: 言愈切，上變色曰：「卿能如此，朕復何憂？」

translations.literal: His words grew more pressing; the emperor changed color and said: "Minister, able to be thus—what further worry have We?"
translations.idiomatic: His words grew fiercer. The emperor's face changed. "If you speak thus," he said, "what have I to fear?"

sentences.zh: 內侍請上易衣，上卻之曰：「留以旌直臣。」

translations.literal: Inner attendants asked the emperor to change robes; he refused, saying: "Keep them to honor a straight minister."
translations.idiomatic: Attendants urged a change of robe; the emperor refused: "Leave it to commemorate an honest remonstrator."

sentences.zh: 翌日，貫等相率前訴，謂國家極治，安得此不詳語。

translations.literal: The next day Guan and others in succession came forward to complain, saying the state was in utmost order—how could there be such inauspicious words.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Tong Guan and his circle filed complaints, insisting the realm was perfectly governed and calling such speech ill-omened.

sentences.zh: 盧航奏禾狂妄，謫監信州酒。

translations.literal: Lu Hang memorialized that He was arrogant and reckless; he was demoted to supervise Xinzhou wine.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Hang memorialized that He was reckless; he was banished to supervise the state wine monopoly at Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 遇赦，得自便還里。

translations.literal: He met an amnesty and was permitted to return home at his convenience.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty allowed him to return home.

sentences.zh: 初，陳瓘歸自嶺外，居於鄞，與禾相好，遣其子正匯從學。

translations.literal: Earlier Chen Guan returned from beyond the Ling and dwelt at Yin, friendly with He, sending his son Zhenghui to study with him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Chen Guan, back from exile in the far south, settled at Yin, befriended He, and sent his son Zhenghui to study under him.

sentences.zh: 後正匯告京罪，執詣闕，瓘亦就逮。

translations.literal: Later Zhenghui reported Jing's crimes, was seized and taken to the palace gate; Guan was also arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhenghui denounced Cai Jing's crimes and was marched to the capital; Guan was arrested as well.

sentences.zh: 經臣蒞其獄，檄禾取證，禾答以事有之，罪不敢逃。

translations.literal: Jingchen presided over the case, sent a dispatch ordering He to testify; He answered that the matter was so and he dared not escape guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jingchen presided over the trial and summoned He to testify. He admitted the facts and refused to evade blame.

sentences.zh: 或謂其失對，禾曰：「禍福死生，命也，豈可以死易不義耶？

translations.literal: Some called his reply a failure; He said: "Fortune, calamity, death, and life are fate—how can one trade death for unrighteousness?
translations.idiomatic: Some said he had answered badly. He said, "Life and death are ordained. How can I buy off injustice with my life?

sentences.zh: 願得分賢者罪。」

translations.literal: I wish to take a share of the worthy man's guilt."
translations.idiomatic: I would gladly share the punishment of a worthy man."

sentences.zh: 遂坐瓘黨停官。

translations.literal: He was then convicted as Guan's partisan and his office was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed as a partisan of Chen Guan.

sentences.zh: 遇赦，復起知廣德軍，移知和州。

translations.literal: He met an amnesty, was restored and made military prefect of Guangde, then transferred to Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty restored him; he governed Guangde Army, then Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 尋遭內艱，服除，知秀州。

translations.literal: Soon he suffered inner bereavement; when mourning ended he governed Xiuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then mourned his mother; after the mourning period he was made prefect of Xiuzhou.

sentences.zh: 王黼新得政，禾曰：「安能出黼門下？」

translations.literal: Wang Fu had newly come to power; He said: "How can I emerge from under Fu's gate?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Fu newly rose to power, He said, "How can I serve under Wang Fu's patronage?"

sentences.zh: 力辭，改汝州。

translations.literal: He forcefully declined and was changed to Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed his refusal and was reassigned to Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 辭益堅，曰：「寧餓死。」

translations.literal: His refusal grew firmer; he said: "I would rather starve."
translations.idiomatic: He refused all the more firmly: "I would rather starve."

sentences.zh: 黼聞而銜之。

translations.literal: Fu heard and harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu took offense.

sentences.zh: 禾兄秉時為壽春府教授，禾侍兄官居。

translations.literal: His elder brother Bingshi was professor at Shouchun Prefecture; He resided attending his brother's official post.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Bingshi served as academic instructor at Shouchun; He lived with him in his official quarters.

sentences.zh: 適童貫領兵道府下，謁不得入，饋之不受。

translations.literal: Just then Tong Guan led troops passing below the prefecture; He could not obtain an audience and would not accept gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guan happened to lead troops past the prefecture. He denied him an audience and refused his gifts.

sentences.zh: 貫怒，歸而譖之，上曰：「此人素如此，汝不能容邪？」

translations.literal: Guan was angry, returned and slandered him; the emperor said: "This man has always been thus—can you not tolerate him?"
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guan complained to the throne. The emperor said, "He has always been this way—can you not bear him?"

sentences.zh: 久之，知舒州，命下而 卒，贈中大夫，諡文介。

translations.literal: After long time he was made prefect of Shuzhou; the order came down and he died; posthumously gifted Grand Master of Palace Attendance, posthumous name Wénjiè.
translations.idiomatic: At length he was appointed prefect of Shuzhou but died before taking up the post. He was posthumously honored as Grand Master of Palace Attendance with the posthumous title Wénjiè (Cultured and Upright).

sentences.zh: 禾性不苟合，立朝挺挺有風操。

translations.literal: His nature did not lightly accommodate; standing at court he was stiffly upright with moral bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He would not trim to others' convenience; in office he stood rigidly upright in character.

sentences.zh: 有《易傳》九卷，《春秋傳》十二卷，《論語》、《孟子解》各十卷。

translations.literal: He had nine scrolls Commentary on the Changes, twelve scrolls Commentary on the Spring and Autumn, ten scrolls each Exegesis of the Analects and Mencius.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included a nine-scroll Commentary on the Changes, a twelve-scroll Commentary on the Spring and Autumn, and ten-scroll exegeses each of the Analects and Mencius.

sentences.zh: 蔣猷，字仲遠，潤州金壇縣人。

translations.literal: Jiang You, style Zhongyuan, a native of Jintan County in Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang You, courtesy name Zhongyuan, was from Jintan in Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 政和四年，拜御史中丞兼侍讀，有直聲。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenghe he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief with concurrent Palace Reader, with a reputation for uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1114 he became Vice Censor-in-Chief and Palace Reader, earning a name for fearless speech.

sentences.zh: 嘗論士風浮薄，廷臣伺人主意，承宰執風旨向背，以特立不回者為愚，共嗤笑 之，此風不可長；

translations.literal: He once discussed that scholar ethos was frivolous and thin, court ministers watched others' intent, received chief ministers' wind and bent to or from them, taking those who stood alone unmoved as foolish—all mocked together; this wind must not be allowed to grow;
translations.idiomatic: He once deplored how shallow court morals had grown: officials read their superiors' moods, took their cue from the chief ministers' preferences, and mocked anyone who stood alone as a fool—such habits, he said, must not be indulged;

sentences.zh: 輔臣奏事殿上，雷同唱和，略無所可否，非論道獻替之禮；

translations.literal: assisting ministers memorialized on the hall, chiming in identical accord, scarcely assenting or dissenting—this was not the rite of discussing the Way and offering replacements;
translations.idiomatic: that when chief ministers reported to the throne they chorused agreement without true debate, violating the rite of frank counsel;

sentences.zh: 內侍省不隸台察，紊元豐官制；

translations.literal: the Inner Palace Service was not subordinate to censorate oversight, disordering the Yuanfeng official system;
translations.idiomatic: that the Inner Palace Service escaped censorial oversight, marring the Yuanfeng bureaucratic order;

sentences.zh: 楊戩不當除節度使；

translations.literal: Yang Jian should not be cleared as military commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: that Yang Jian should not have been made a military commissioner;

sentences.zh: 趙良嗣不宜出入禁中。

translations.literal: Zhao Liangsi was unsuited to entering and leaving the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: and that Zhao Liangsi had no business coming and going within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 上皆嘉納， 至揭其章內侍省，且詔自今無得規圖節鉞。

translations.literal: The emperor all praised and accepted, even posting his memorial at the Inner Palace Service, and edicting that from now on they must not scheme for command seals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted every point, posted his memorial inside the Inner Palace Service, and decreed that eunuchs must never again seek military commissions.

sentences.zh: 又疏孟昌齡、徐鑄等奸狀。

translations.literal: He again detailed the villainous conduct of Meng Changling, Xu Zhu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He also exposed the corrupt dealings of Meng Changling, Xu Zhu, and others.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部尚書兼禮制局詳議官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of War with concurrent detailed deliberator of the Rites Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of War and detailed deliberator of the Rites Reform Bureau.

sentences.zh: 七年，知貢舉，改工部、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he supervised the metropolitan examination, was changed to Minister of Works and Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he oversaw the metropolitan examination, then became Minister of Works and Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 以徽猷閣直學士知婺州。

translations.literal: As Academician Expositor of the Hall of Lofty Principles he governed Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As Academician of the Hall of Lofty Principles he governed Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，請祠歸。

translations.literal: The next year he requested a shrine appointment and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he sought a temple posting and retired home.

sentences.zh: 宣和末，召為刑部尚書兼資善堂翊善。

translations.literal: At the end of Xuanhe he was summoned as Minister of Punishments with concurrent Companion at the Hall of Exemplary Worth.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Xuanhe era he was recalled as Minister of Justice and companion to the Heir Apparent at the Hall of Exemplary Worth.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，奉上表起居太上皇帝于淮陰，且特詔貶童貫。

translations.literal: At the start of Jingkang he presented a memorial of daily greeting to the retired emperor at Huaiyin, and moreover a special edict demoted Tong Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingkang crisis he attended the Retired Emperor at Huaiyin and won a special edict demoting Tong Guan.

sentences.zh: 猷奏貫得罪天下，願黜遠 之。

translations.literal: You memorialized that Guan had offended all under Heaven and wished him demoted far away.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang You memorialized that Tong Guan had forfeited the world's trust and begged his banishment to the far marches.

sentences.zh: 太上以為然，亟令宣詔，趣貫赴貶所。

translations.literal: The retired emperor thought it right and urgently ordered the edict proclaimed, hurrying Guan to his place of demotion.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor agreed and at once proclaimed the edict, pressing Tong Guan to his place of exile.

sentences.zh: 遂奉太上還京，移兵部尚書，累官正議大夫。

translations.literal: He then escorted the retired emperor back to the capital, was moved to Minister of War, and accumulated office to Rectifying Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: He then escorted the Retired Emperor to the capital, was made Minister of War again, and rose to Rectifying Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 引疾，授徽猷閣直學士、提舉嵩山崇福宮。

translations.literal: He cited illness; was granted Academician Expositor of the Hall of Lofty Principles and Commissioner to Oversee the Chongfu Palace on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: Citing illness, he was granted academician rank and made overseer of the Chongfu Palace on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 贈特進。

translations.literal: Posthumously gifted Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 論曰：夫拯溺救焚之際，必以任人為急。

translations.literal: Commentary says: In the emergency of rescuing the drowning and saving from fire, employing men must be urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: When the realm is drowning in flame, nothing matters more than putting the right men in place.

sentences.zh: 靖康、建炎之禍變，亦甚於焚溺矣。

translations.literal: The disasters and changes of Jingkang and Jianyan also exceed burning and drowning.
translations.idiomatic: The calamities of Jingkang and Jianyan were worse than any flood or fire.

sentences.zh: 當時非乏人才也，然而國恥卒不能雪者，豈非任之之道有所未至歟？

translations.literal: At that time talent was not lacking, yet national shame in the end could not be washed away—is it not that the way of employing them had not fully reached?
translations.idiomatic: The empire was not short of talent, yet national shame went unavenged—was this not because men were not truly entrusted with power to act?

sentences.zh: 夫以李光之才 識高明，所至有聲；

translations.literal: As for Li Guang's talent and insight, lofty and bright—wherever he went there was renown;
translations.idiomatic: Li Guang was gifted and farsighted and won acclaim wherever he served;

sentences.zh: 許翰、許景衡之論議剴切；

translations.literal: Xu Han and Xu Jingheng's discourse sharp and cutting;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Han and Xu Jingheng spoke with piercing force;

sentences.zh: 張愨之善理財；

translations.literal: Zhang Que's skill at managing finances;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Que excelled at finance;

sentences.zh: 張所之習知河北利害：皆一時之雋也。

translations.literal: Zhang Suo's thorough knowledge of Hebei's profit and harm—all were outstanding men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Suo knew the strategic situation in Hebei through and through: each was a leading man of his day.

sentences.zh: 是數臣者，使其言聽計從，不為讒邪所抑，得以直行其志，其 效宜可待也。

translations.literal: These several ministers—if their words were heard and plans followed, not suppressed by slanderous villainy, able to go straight with their will—their effect should await realization.
translations.idiomatic: Had these men been heeded and not thwarted by slander, allowed to carry out their aims, results should have followed in due course.

sentences.zh: 然或斥遠以死，或用之不竟其才，世之治亂安危，雖非人力所為，君子于此，則不能無咎于時君之失政焉。

translations.literal: Yet some were dismissed to distant places and died, or employed but their talent not brought to completion; the age's order, disorder, safety, and peril—though not wholly within human power—upon this the gentleman cannot be without fault toward the ruler of the time's misgovernment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet some were exiled to die in obscurity, others used but never to the full; though fortune governs empires, the cultivated man cannot wholly excuse the ruler's failure to employ them rightly.

sentences.zh: 蔣猷曆仕五朝，當建炎初，避地而終，則無 足稱也。

translations.literal: Jiang You served through five reigns; at the start of Jianyan he avoided the land and ended—then there is nothing worth praising.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang You served five reigns, fled when Jianyan began, and died in retirement—little here to commend.

sentences.zh: 陳禾引裾盡言，有古諫臣之風，其行事在宣和之前，孝宗以後乃加褒諡云。

translations.literal: Chen He pulled the robe hem and spoke to the end, having the wind of ancient remonstrating ministers; his conduct was before Xuanhe, and only after Xiaozong was posthumous praise and investiture added.
translations.idiomatic: Chen He seized the emperor's robe and spoke his fill in the manner of remonstrators of old; his deeds antedated Xuanhe, and only under Xiaozong was he finally honored with a posthumous title.
